a2.speaker: João Lourenço, Angolan President
a2.name: João Lourenço
a2.title: Angolan President
a2.speech: "It is time to replace the logic of aid with the logic of investment and trade." ; Urged US companies to diversify beyond traditional oil and mineral extraction and invest in sectors such as automotive manufacturing, shipbuilding, tourism, cement production and steel production.

a2.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, African Union Commission Chairperson
a2.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a2.title: African Union Commission Chairperson
a2.speech: "We're not seeking aid, but building co-created solutions." ; Called for the removal of punitive tariffs and visa restrictions, noting that Africa's 1.3 billion people and abundant resources remain among the world's most significant untapped economic opportunities ; "This should not just be a summit, but a call to action. Together, let's walk the pathways to prosperity—with unity, purpose and Agenda 2063 as our guide."

a2.speaker: Dr Akinwumi Adesina, African Development Bank Group President
a2.name: Dr Akinwumi Adesina
a2.title: African Development Bank Group President
a2.speech: "We should review the high tariffs on African countries. What is needed is more trade between Africa and the US, not less." ; Pointed to the Lobito corridor as a concrete example of strategic investment already underway ; "That is why the African Development Bank is a key strategic partner with the U.S., Angola, and Zambia on the development of the Lobito corridor."

a2.speaker: Wamkele Mene, African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretary General
a2.name: Wamkele Mene
a2.title: African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretary General
a2.speech: "The undertaking of the AfCFTA is an ambitious one—It has to be ambitious." ; Emphasised that the success of AfCFTA is essential to scale investment, reduce fragmentation and accelerate industrial development across the continent.

a2.speaker: Troy Fitrell, Senior State Department Bureau Official
a2.name: Troy Fitrell
a2.title: Senior State Department Bureau Official
a2.speech: "There are business leaders in the US who need to understand the opportunities that lie in doing business with Africa. Our mission going forward will be to find them—and bring them in."

a61.speaker: Dr Khumo Seipone, CEO of the African Comprehensive HIV/AIDS Partnerships (ACHAP), former Director of Health Services at Botswana's Ministry of Health
a61.name: Dr Khumo Seipone
a61.title: CEO of the African Comprehensive HIV/AIDS Partnerships (ACHAP), former Director of Health Services at Botswana's Ministry of Health
a61.speech: Disclosed that if the government had not disregarded the 2017 national policy guidelines on social contracting for NGOs, many NGOs would not be as stranded, underfunded, and fighting for survival as they currently are in the wake of recent foreign aid cuts. Said "each government ministry was expected to create sector-specific funding plans to support NGOs involved in expanding government programs." Lamented the lost opportunity, stressing that "had the government implemented the guidelines, Botswana would not be in its current predicament where NGOs are struggling to stay afloat due to diminishing foreign aid." Said the warning signs of an impending disaster were always evident but were ignored, noting that even PEPFAR, a key partner in health funding, had been reducing its support by between 10 and 14 percent annually. Said "international funding models require governments to equally co-fund global initiatives, which is something that Botswana had failed to do over the years and what led to the collapse of many NGOs in critical sectors like health and education." Asked how the co-funding was to be achieved, said "ministries were advised to develop sector-specific priorities, engage NGOs and look into possibilities of using levies, among other means, to support NGOs, which are actually doing the work on behalf of the government."

a61.speaker: Dr Khumo Seipone, CEO of the African Comprehensive HIV/AIDS Partnerships (ACHAP)
a61.name: Dr Khumo Seipone
a61.title: CEO of the African Comprehensive HIV/AIDS Partnerships (ACHAP)
a61.speech: Said one of the reasons Botswana's NGOs are struggling is that the private sector is not supportive. Said "In the past, the private sector has openly told us that there is need for policy and legal reforms to encourage collaboration between the private sector and NGOs, to drive social and community development. They want tax incentives. In developed countries, private sector support for NGOs is facilitated through tax incentives, regulatory support, public-private partnerships, and corporate social responsibility programmes, among others. The time has come for us to bring them on board because the government can't do it alone."

a61.speaker: Professor Oatlhokwa Nkomazana, Permanent Secretary, Botswana Ministry of Health
a61.name: Professor Oatlhokwa Nkomazana
a61.title: Permanent Secretary, Botswana Ministry of Health
a61.speech: Acknowledged the issue and promised to revisit the matter. Said "I am aware of the concerns raised by Dr Seipone regarding funding of NGOs and sustainability. Unfortunately, I was not yet with the ministry when these national guidelines were established and don't know much about them. But I will make time to familiarise myself with them."

a61.speaker: Ministry of Health of Botswana
a61.name: Ministry of Health of Botswana
a61.speech: Reassured the public that they have the situation under control; has already met with civil society representatives to discuss a course for the future. Committed to doing everything possible to protect essential services.

a287.speaker: Captain Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso and Head of State (official speech delivered by Minister of the Economy and Finance Aboubakar Nacanabo)
a287.name: Captain Ibrahim Traore
a287.title: President of Faso and Head of State (official speech delivered by Minister of the Economy and Finance Aboubakar Nacanabo)
a287.speech: Welcomed the birth of the Postal Bank of Burkina Faso, which forms part of his vision of "inclusive development, economic and social progress from which every Burkinabe will be able to benefit" ; said this institution is not merely a bank but embodies the aspirations of the people in search of greater well-being, which will come about thanks to the financing of the strategic sectors of the economy ; said the bank, alongside the Treasury Deposit Bank and the Deposit and Investment Fund, will play "a crucial role in the centralisation of public resources and the financing of structuring projects, thus contributing to the economic transformation of our country".

a287.speaker: Captain Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso (entry in the bank's guest book)
a287.name: Captain Ibrahim Traore
a287.title: President of Faso (entry in the bank's guest book)
a287.speech: Invited the staff to make the BPBF a local financial institution that will support development everywhere in Burkina Faso.

a287.speaker: Inoussa Boundaone, Managing Director of the Postal Bank of Burkina Faso (BPBF)
a287.name: Inoussa Boundaone
a287.title: Managing Director of the Postal Bank of Burkina Faso (BPBF)
a287.speech: Welcomed the efforts of the Head of State and of the government for their involvement in bringing the bank effectively into operation ; said the BPBF, which took its first steps in the banking world in April 2023, is "the fruit of a collective effort, guided by a strong conviction, that of bringing banking services closer to citizens, wherever they may be" ; said the bank reflects the shareholders' commitment to offering financial services adapted to the needs of the population in order to strengthen financial inclusion.

a391.speaker: National Competitiveness Commission (NCC)
a391.name: National Competitiveness Commission (NCC)
a391.speech: According to the NCC, the dairy sector is a significant employer, providing direct jobs to 30,000 people and indirectly to 1.3 million households, and national annual milk production increased by 52.5 per cent from 75.4 million litres in 2018 to about 115 million litres in 2024, against an estimated national demand of about 130 million litres per annum; the NCC says the resulting gap of about 15 million litres is being supplemented by imported raw milk from Mozambique and powdered milk from India and South Africa, among others.

a391.speaker: Dairy Sector Strategic Plan (2021-2025)
a391.name: Dairy Sector Strategic Plan (2021-2025)
a391.speech: According to the plan, Zimbabwe produced over 260 million litres per year at its peak during the early 1990s.

a391.speaker: Zimbabwe Association of Dairy Farmers (ZADF)
a391.name: Zimbabwe Association of Dairy Farmers (ZADF)
a391.speech: According to the ZADF, at its inception the Marirangwe milk collection centre used to produce an average of 9,000 litres per month and now, with increased production, it is the largest of the MCCs in terms of milk procurement from farmer aggregators.

a391.speaker: William Mazingi, Marirangwe Dairy Farmers Association secretary and dairy farmer
a391.name: William Mazingi
a391.title: Marirangwe Dairy Farmers Association secretary and dairy farmer
a391.speech: "Our milk target for the year 2025-2026 is one million litres of milk, up from 773 962 litres of milk last year," adding the MCC plans to venture into value addition and start producing cheese, yoghurt and other dairy products ; "By working together, we have been able to leverage on collective bargaining power to secure more favourable deals with milk processors and distributors," adding, "Government supported us with inputs to grow silage and this has increased milk production in the past three years."

a391.speaker: Antonnette Chingwe, ZADF Principal Policy Officer
a391.name: Antonnette Chingwe
a391.title: ZADF Principal Policy Officer
a391.speech: Said the gap in supply is an opportunity for smallholder dairy farmers to increase household agricultural incomes.

a391.speaker: Takudzwa Chimuto, ZADF Dairy Revitalisation Program Officer
a391.name: Takudzwa Chimuto
a391.title: ZADF Dairy Revitalisation Program Officer
a391.speech: "The country is also importing high-quality semen to enhance dairy genetics."

a391.speaker: Dr Renneth Mano, Livestock and Meat Advisory Council Executive Administrator
a391.name: Dr Renneth Mano
a391.title: Livestock and Meat Advisory Council Executive Administrator
a391.speech: "The dairy sector growth signals not only the strength of current interventions but also the sector's potential to reach full self-sufficiency. Now more than ever, it's crucial to consolidate these gains by scaling up support mechanisms, addressing sector-specific needs, and unlocking financing to future-proof dairy production." ; Added that with the national requirement standing at 130 million litres per annum, Zimbabwe is gradually closing the gap and reducing its reliance on imports.

a614.speaker: A growing body of research
a614.name: A growing body of research
a614.speech: According to a growing body of research, artificial intelligence (AI) can perform a range of tasks that were previously the sole purview of qualified doctors.

a614.speaker: Several recent studies on AI detection software
a614.name: Several recent studies on AI detection software
a614.speech: Show that more tumours can be found during routine breast x-rays and colonoscopies when AI detection software assists in scanning images.

a614.speaker: Researchers at Google (study)
a614.name: Researchers at Google (study)
a614.speech: Tested whether large language models can correctly diagnose patients, and found that an AI model that they developed could provide a list of possible diagnoses for real-world patients that were significantly more accurate than those offered by doctors who were provided with the exact same information.

a614.speaker: Dr Emily Wong, infectious disease scientist at the African Health Research Institute
a614.name: Dr Emily Wong
a614.title: infectious disease scientist at the African Health Research Institute
a614.speech: Explains that "you have to interpret those chest X-rays, and usually that requires a doctor or even a radiologist - which is a medical specialist - and [they] are very scarce in South Africa."

a614.speaker: 2021 study of AI-based CAD software
a614.name: 2021 study of AI-based CAD software
a614.speech: Showed that a series of AI-based software applications were not only able to detect TB in X-ray images as accurately as experienced radiologists, but were actually outperforming them ; found that at a threshold score of 60, the top performing CAD tool, called qXR, captured 90% of TB cases, while 74% of TB-negative people were correctly categorised as negative, compared with human radiologists who only captured about 89% of cases and classified 63% of the TB-negative people correctly.

a614.speaker: Dr Emily Wong and colleagues (TB screening project in northern KwaZulu-Natal)
a614.name: Dr Emily Wong and colleagues (TB screening project in northern KwaZulu-Natal)
a614.speech: Tested one of these AI products in a TB screening project in northern KwaZulu-Natal and found that the software was roughly as accurate as doctors.

a614.speaker: Dr Jody Boffa, scientist at the TB Think Tank, which advises the National Department of Health
a614.name: Dr Jody Boffa
a614.title: scientist at the TB Think Tank, which advises the National Department of Health
a614.speech: Explains: "Global Fund and USAID fund the machines, but then a variety of implementing agencies [typically NGOs] are actually taking them out into the field." ; says the health department "sets the rules" for how these programmes should operate.

a614.speaker: Dr Elias Ramarumo, National Department of Health official monitoring the projects
a614.name: Dr Elias Ramarumo
a614.title: National Department of Health official monitoring the projects
a614.speech: Tells Spotlight that 38 CAD software products had been procured by Global Fund, while eight were bought by USAID ; notes that provincial health departments were "in a process of procuring digital X-ray units", which will "come with CAD software" ; adds that both companies are working with South African partners: Delft is working with Lomaen Medical, while Qure.AI is working with Vertice MedTech.

a614.speaker: Dr Jody Boffa, scientist at the TB Think Tank
a614.name: Dr Jody Boffa
a614.title: scientist at the TB Think Tank
a614.speech: Notes that two CAD products are currently being purchased by funders - CAD4TB, owned by a Dutch company called Delft, and qXR by the Indian venture, Qure.AI ; says the products are being used in two kinds of screening programmes: vans containing mobile X-ray devices parked next to overburdened clinics, and vans taken to "hotspot" communities, placed in areas "where people that are less likely to come to the clinic would be found", with project staff or community leaders "rally[ing] the area to let them know that they'll be coming in" before the vans arrive.

a614.speaker: National Department of Health (South Africa)
a614.name: National Department of Health (South Africa)
a614.speech: Says that it's also planning on using CAD software - not only for tackling TB but also for silicosis.

a614.speaker: Professor Rodney Ehrlich, occupational medicine specialist at UCT
a614.name: Professor Rodney Ehrlich
a614.title: occupational medicine specialist at UCT
a614.speech: Says the Medical Bureau for Occupational Disease hasn't always been able to manage claims fast enough: "By about a decade ago, the completion backlog [of unpaid compensation claims] was over a hundred thousand, and all these paper files were piled up in back offices." ; says getting through claims requires enormous staffing capacity, because a panel of doctors is required to analyse each X-ray image - the opinion of one doctor isn't considered good enough.

a614.speaker: 2022 study co-authored by Rodney Ehrlich
a614.name: 2022 study co-authored by Rodney Ehrlich
a614.speech: Analysed the ability of CAD software to detect silicosis and TB in chest X-ray images of North West gold miners, and found that despite concerns that the AI would not be able to distinguish between the two diseases, the CAD products were able to make similar classifications as those made by doctors.

a614.speaker: Dr Elias Ramarumo, National Department of Health
a614.name: Dr Elias Ramarumo
a614.title: National Department of Health
a614.speech: Says the health department and its partners hosted a workshop in June designed to "forge a way towards harnessing AI" for silicosis and TB screening in "mining, peri mining and labour-sending communities of SA" ; says it was agreed "the adoption of CAD systems for TB and silicosis in the mining sector is essential to enhance diagnostic accuracy, improve patient outcomes, enhance the compensation process and reduce the financial burden on the [mining] industry".

a614.speaker: Dr Emily Wong, infectious disease scientist at the African Health Research Institute
a614.name: Dr Emily Wong
a614.title: infectious disease scientist at the African Health Research Institute
a614.speech: Explains that "the original paradigm... is that someone with TB is highly symptomatic - they have fevers, they've been coughing for weeks, they've lost a lot of weight, they're sick - they've now come to seek care and they've been diagnosed with TB" ; says that when CAD is trained on banks of chest X-rays, the images labelled "TB" will be from people who were highly symptomatic, so the CAD software only learns to associate the disease with more extreme cases.

a614.speaker: Dr Emily Wong and colleagues (statement released last year)
a614.name: Dr Emily Wong and colleagues (statement released last year)
a614.speech: Released a statement last year which called for "regulation to require CAD-developing companies to communicate changes between software versions".

a614.speaker: 2022 journal article on medical device regulation
a614.name: 2022 journal article on medical device regulation
a614.speech: Argued that existing legislation is outdated for reviewing AI-based technologies, one issue in particular being that the safety and efficacy of a device is supposed to be reviewed according to "predefined static specifications and standards".

a614.speaker: Nthabi Moloi, communications officer of the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (Sahpra)
a614.name: Nthabi Moloi
a614.title: communications officer of the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (Sahpra)
a614.speech: Told Spotlight that the body "has not commenced with the registration of medical devices".

a614.speaker: Zhi Zhen Qin, digital health specialist at the United Nations Office for Project Service
a614.name: Zhi Zhen Qin
a614.title: digital health specialist at the United Nations Office for Project Service
a614.speech: Says she was "impressed by the vision" of the conference organisers, and that by aiming to use AI to screen for both TB and silicosis at the same time - instead of viewing them as separate problems - "the South African government has been filling a much-needed leadership gap".

a641.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a641.name: Joseph Boakai
a641.title: President of Liberia
a641.speech: says Liberia’s development drive is now, and there should be no room for excuses: “As we gather here today to endorse Liberia’s new development plan – the Arrest Agenda for Inclusive Development or AAID, let us be reminded that now is the time for all of us to work collaboratively to develop this country; no time for an excuse.” ; “As we come together to endorse the rest of the Agenda for Inclusive Development, AAID, and the Counter-Development Agenda, we are doing so when we are beginning to see the signs of common progress in our country.” ; expressed delight in presiding over what he describes as an inspiring moment in his government’s journey to rescuing Liberia.

a641.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a641.name: Joseph Boakai
a641.title: President of Liberia
a641.speech: says it is no secret that Liberia faces significant challenges, including food insecurity, better nutrition, and a near-persistent lack of access to essential services such as clean drinking water, reliable electricity, adequate housing, and health care: “Our people deserve better, and our responsibility is to address these challenges head-on.”

a641.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a641.name: Joseph Boakai
a641.title: President of Liberia
a641.speech: Said the AAID is part of a comprehensive strategy supported by an ambitious program to tackle multidimensional poverty and create a lasting environment in citizens’ lives: “Our focus is diversifying the economy, building resilient infrastructure, strengthening the rule of law, improving governance, combating corruption, ensuring environmental sustainability, ensuring ecological security, and investing in the human capital.” ; names agribusiness, infrastructure, the rule of law, and governance as key development drivers, adding that agribusiness, infrastructure, the rule of law, education, human capital, sanitation, and tourism are areas critical to Liberia’s future ; “My government is taking a proactive role in Liberia’s development through education and other areas; we are committed to championing the flagship projects central to the AAID. However, let me be very clear: these are not the only projects for the AAID, but others will also support the development through the ARREST project in Liberia.”

a641.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a641.name: Joseph Boakai
a641.title: President of Liberia
a641.speech: says many sectorial, county-level initiatives will be implemented by all stakeholders, and that the government will also work closely with development partners, the private sector, civil society, and citizens both here and in the diaspora to ensure the effective implementation of the AAID plan ; “I urge all of you to engage fully and contribute your expertise as we move forward,” calling on his officials to commit to a culture of mutual accountability ; notes that “the success of this agenda” depends on the government managing its limited resources and ensuring they are judiciously used effectively and efficiently, thereby impacting development and improving livelihoods.

a641.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a641.name: Joseph Boakai
a641.title: President of Liberia
a641.speech: Said the AAID is a call to action for all Liberians: government, private sector, international partners, civil society, and communities, and a call to unite in a shared vision for a prosperous and equitable Liberia: “Collaboration will be vital to revitalizing peace sectors such as agribusiness, tourism, digital technology, infrastructure, education, and health care.” ; says officials must ensure it is not limited to economic growth, but tangible development that benefits every Liberian, requiring decisive actions to address corruption, tackle governance challenges, and leverage technology to improve public service delivery.

a641.speaker: Christine N. Umutoni, United Nations Resident Coordinator to Liberia
a641.name: Christine N. Umutoni
a641.title: United Nations Resident Coordinator to Liberia
a641.speech: says it is a pleasure for the government to have included international partners in its development plan for 2025-2029, dubbed the Arrest Agenda for Inclusive Development and the 15 County Development Agendas ; on behalf of development partners, the UN, and friends of Liberia, she congratulates the government and the people of Liberia for reaching this important milestone ; “Mr. President, we know very well that Liberia’s journey, with the government and the people leading their development agenda, but we also are aware that partnership, collaboration, and coordination are vital for everything to come together coherently towards common objectives; no single entity can achieve this.” ; calls for a united effort across government institutions, private sector, civil society, diaspora, and all development partners to achieve the plan ; pledges, “We will continue to align our programs with Liberia’s priorities, ensuring synergy and maximum development impact.” ; adds that it is among the few plans being designed for 2029, basically towards the end of the SDGs circle.

a664.speaker: Me Jean Samandari, president and legal representative of the ACP (Association Action Contre la Pauvrete)
a664.name: Me Jean Samandari
a664.title: president and legal representative of the ACP (Association Action Contre la Pauvrete)
a664.speech: Announced that the initiative was set up so that people on low incomes could enjoy good health in order to progress and not be left behind in achieving the National Vision 2040-2060, and that it was organised with the aim of helping access to health care and implementing ministerial ordinance number 630/540/1021 of 7 February 2025, whose article 2 stipulates that possessing a CAM is compulsory ; reported that, faced with the difficulties encountered by vulnerable families, the ACP decided to take part in this government programme aimed at guaranteeing good health for all, by helping up to 1,500 low-income families in Ntahangwa commune and elsewhere: "In addition to providing CAMs, we will also provide them with cards allowing them to access an ambulance free of charge." ; expressed his gratitude to those who made the activity possible, in particular the New Africa Fund association, and asked beneficiaries to consult doctors without hesitation when health problems arise.

a664.speaker: Steve Habiyambere, representative of the US-based supporters of the ACP initiative
a664.name: Steve Habiyambere
a664.title: representative of the US-based supporters of the ACP initiative
a664.speech: Asked everyone to remember people in precarious situations so that they too may enjoy good health: "We must remember that a person possesses wealth by chance, and that it is important for them to remember that their contribution is necessary so that everyone can have good health."

a664.speaker: Bazompora Alexis, representative of the Twa families who received medical assistance cards
a664.name: Bazompora Alexis
a664.title: representative of the Twa families who received medical assistance cards
a664.speech: Said he was very happy with the assistance provided to preserve their health, and explained that many Twa families have low incomes but that the support they receive encourages them not to be left behind in development.

a664.speaker: Diane Kwizera, economic and socio-cultural adviser of Ntahangwa commune (representing the administrator)
a664.name: Diane Kwizera
a664.title: economic and socio-cultural adviser of Ntahangwa commune (representing the administrator)
a664.speech: Expressed her gratitude for the ACP's honourable act, recalled that people must always help one another so that the country can achieve the National Vision 2040-2060, and reminded administrative officials to mobilise citizens so that every person who has reached the age of 18 possesses a medical assistance card.

a1039.speaker: UNECA (statement released on Friday)
a1039.name: UNECA (statement released on Friday)
a1039.speech: reported that the Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa, Claver Gatete, has blamed rising debt, geopolitical instability and declining aid flows for putting African economies under pressure.

a1039.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1039.name: Claver Gatete
a1039.title: Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1039.speech: highlighted the economic pressures on African countries with many of them facing debt distress, inflation and trade disruptions driven by global policy shifts: “Real GDP across the continent is projected to grow between 2.9 percent and 3.6 percent,” noting that over half of African countries now carry public debt exceeding 60 percent of GDP ; “Seven are officially in debt distress, while 11 more are considered at high risk.”

a1039.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1039.name: Claver Gatete
a1039.title: Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1039.speech: said steep currency depreciation, inflation and widening current account deficits have deepened the strain ; “External financing is drying up, but the pressure on government budgets keeps growing. We cannot overstate the urgency of domestic resource mobilisation.”

a1039.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1039.name: Claver Gatete
a1039.title: Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1039.speech: warned that Africa's exposure to global volatility is deepening, noting official development assistance dropped to 2.1 per cent of GNI in 2023, down from 3.4 per cent in 2006, and that major donors, including the United States, United Kingdom and Germany, have announced further cuts.

a1039.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1039.name: Claver Gatete
a1039.title: Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
a1039.speech: “This goes beyond trade volumes. It affects industrial jobs, regional supply chains and Africa's voice in shaping the terms of engagement.”

a1039.speaker: Forthcoming joint research by ECA, the African Union Commission and the African Development Bank
a1039.name: Forthcoming joint research by ECA
a1039.title: the African Union Commission and the African Development Bank
a1039.speech: suggests that new United States import tariffs could reduce Africa's exports to the United States by up to 21.5 percent.

a1156.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) in Sudan (statement)
a1156.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) in Sudan (statement)
a1156.speech: Welcomes a contribution of EUR6.55 million from the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS); according to a statement on Monday this vital funding will enable WFP to provide specialised nutritious foods and cash-based nutrition assistance to nearly 200,000 young children and pregnant or nursing women in Gedaref and Kassala states ; "This support will help prevent malnutrition in eastern Sudan, which is critical as some 3.7 million children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding mothers across the country are malnourished."

a1156.speaker: Laurent Bukera, WFP Regional Director for Eastern Africa
a1156.name: Laurent Bukera
a1156.title: WFP Regional Director for Eastern Africa
a1156.speech: "Amid Sudan's deepening hunger crisis, this generous contribution will help to improve diets among vulnerable women and children, which is key to reducing malnutrition. We are extremely grateful to the Government of Italy."

a1156.speaker: Michele Tommasi, Ambassador of Italy to Sudan
a1156.name: Michele Tommasi
a1156.title: Ambassador of Italy to Sudan
a1156.speech: "With this project, Italy is at the forefront in Sudan in supporting the most vulnerable populations. The partnership with WFP is a tangible example of our commitment in the fight against malnutrition, ensuring access to essential nutritional support for those most in need. This initiative also reflects Italy's broader strategy of humanitarian assistance and sustainable development, reinforcing long-term resilience and food security in the region."

a1156.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a1156.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a1156.speech: Said it is working tirelessly to expand food and nutrition assistance to millions more people across Sudan – aiming to triple the number of people it supports to 7 million.

a1257.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1257.name: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1257.speech: According to OCHA, Somalia continues to face prolonged extreme dry conditions due to the failure of the October-December 2024 rains, leading to worsening humanitarian conditions. The crisis has deepened in Gedo, Hiiraan, Bay, Bakool, Mudug, and Bari, where people struggle to survive under the relentless sun.

a1257.speaker: Representative of Raasamaal Youth Development (local implementing organization, unnamed)
a1257.name: Representative of Raasamaal Youth Development (local implementing organization
a1257.title: unnamed)
a1257.speech: Emphasized the critical impact of the foundation's work: "We received five truckloads of clean water, generously donated by Hassan Kobac Foundation. This support is truly life-saving. In addition to water, HKF has provided essential food rations, including rice, oil, sugar, and dates, to sustain these communities."

a1257.speaker: A beneficiary in Farlibaax (unnamed), speaking to Universal TV
a1257.name: A beneficiary in Farlibaax (unnamed)
a1257.title: speaking to Universal TV
a1257.speech: "We were on the verge of death due to thirst and hunger. But today, thanks to the generosity of Hassan Kobac Foundation, we can see another day with hope."

a1257.speaker: Hassan Idow Muhumed Kobac, founder of the Hassan Kobac Foundation (HKF)
a1257.name: Hassan Idow Muhumed Kobac
a1257.title: founder of the Hassan Kobac Foundation (HKF)
a1257.speech: Speaking on the urgency of the crisis, reaffirmed his foundation's unwavering commitment: "The region has been devastated by this drought, and Farlibaax is among the hardest-hit areas. We have provided what we can as a life-saving measure and will continue to do so, but the need is immense. We must do more."

a1257.speaker: Hon. Mahad Hassan Osman, Deputy Speaker of Hirshabelle Parliament
a1257.name: Hon. Mahad Hassan Osman
a1257.title: Deputy Speaker of Hirshabelle Parliament
a1257.speech: Strongly commended and endorsed the Hassan Kobac Foundation for its unwavering dedication to humanitarian assistance. He urged partners, stakeholders, and development agencies to support and collaborate with this impactful initiative as it continues to shape a brighter future for Somalia's most vulnerable communities.

a1347.speaker: Prof Grace Umezurike, Secretary to the Ebonyi State Government and Co-Chair of the State Transformation Committee (STC)
a1347.name: Prof Grace Umezurike
a1347.title: Secretary to the Ebonyi State Government and Co-Chair of the State Transformation Committee (STC)
a1347.speech: Said the State had gained a lot from the programmes of USAID State2State. She expressed the readiness of government to institutionalize the reforms that would further guarantee good governance and actualization of the people's charter of needs policy of the State. ; Also advocated for the extension of USAID State2State activities in the State, to allow for more capacity building and effective ownership of the reforms that had placed the State on a global map.

a1347.speaker: Chief Mathias Adum, Principal Secretary to the Governor of Ebonyi State
a1347.name: Chief Mathias Adum
a1347.title: Principal Secretary to the Governor of Ebonyi State
a1347.speech: Thanked USAID State2State for their various intervention programmes, trainings and activities aimed at ensuring due process, standard and good governance as been witnessed in the priority sectors. He pledged that his office would continue to collaborate with the OGP team to achieve the objectives of State2State programmes in Ebonyi State.

a1347.speaker: Dr. Sam Onyia, State Team Lead of USAID State2State
a1347.name: Dr. Sam Onyia
a1347.title: State Team Lead of USAID State2State
a1347.speech: Said the joint meeting of the STC and OGP members was to harmonize their plans and activities for a greater synergy in achieving good governance in Ebonyi State. ; "We expect that at the end of this review meeting, the outcome will be a joint action plan for effective coordination and collaboration between STC and OGP towards achieving sustainable development in the State. The State Transformation Committee is State2State's highest organ for promoting public financial management reforms in the state, coordinate governance issues, improving effectiveness, accountability and transparency, especially in priority sectors of primary health, basic education and WASH. The Open Government Partnership (OGP) promotes better relations between the government and the people for transparency and good governance. In Ebonyi, its pillars Fiscal Transparency, Access to Information, Citizens' Engagement, Border Peace and Conflict Management. So, bringing both STC and OGP together is to enhance coordination, collaboration, synergy and sustainability of these reforms. When the two bodies come together to harmonize what they are doing, and have proper collaboration and coordination, the next task would be to achieve consolidation, institutionalization and proper sustainability."

a1347.speaker: Nneka Acholonu Egbunna, USAID State2State Communication Specialist, and Ejiro Okotie, GESI Specialist
a1347.name: Nneka Acholonu Egbunna
a1347.title: USAID State2State Communication Specialist, and Ejiro Okotie, GESI Specialist
a1347.speech: Emphasised that the joint meeting would strengthen the platform for collaboration and synergy between STC and OGP members. They maintained that the two groups would jointly review the STC Reform Sustainability Plan and the OGP State Action plan to ensure that the drivers of these reform plans are working toward the goal of inclusive good governance in Ebonyi State.

a1347.speaker: Chief Oliver Aja Chima, co-chair of OGP and Executive Director of DIG Foundation, and Mr. Eleri Ewa, STC co-chair (represented by Lovenda Nnachi)
a1347.name: Chief Oliver Aja Chima
a1347.title: co-chair of OGP and Executive Director of DIG Foundation, and Mr. Eleri Ewa, STC co-chair (represented by Lovenda Nnachi)
a1347.speech: Said the collaboration between government and civil society organizations (CSOs) have been very fruitful. They noted that the joint review meeting was an important milestone and thanked Ebonyi State government for its commitment to implementing the reforms supported by State2State in the State. They harped on need for greater synergy to improve on the success so far recorded, through consolidation and sustainability plans.

a1459.speaker: Thirty-two African countries, including Presidents Yoweri Museveni of Uganda, Ali Bongo of Gabon and Ian Khama of Botswana (petition)
a1459.name: Thirty-two African countries
a1459.title: including Presidents Yoweri Museveni of Uganda, Ali Bongo of Gabon and Ian Khama of Botswana (petition)
a1459.speech: Wrote a petition calling on the "EU to close its ivory market", calling on the European Union to stop its ivory trade at a conference in Botswana aimed at saving African elephants.

a1459.speaker: Avaaz (global advocacy group)
a1459.name: Avaaz (global advocacy group)
a1459.speech: According to Avaaz, the EU is the world's biggest exporter of legal ivory but that is thought to fuel poaching; according to Avaaz, Britain accounts for the most ivory exported from the EU.

a1459.speaker: Bert Wander, Avaaz campaign director
a1459.name: Bert Wander
a1459.title: Avaaz campaign director
a1459.speech: "What we see is that Europe has become both a destination and transit hub for illegal ivory." ; "It's crucial that this trade is shut down if we're going to protect these magnificent animals". ; "The rest of the world is turning its back on ivory trade. Why not Europe?"

a1459.speaker: EU officials (anonymous, as relayed by Bert Wander of Avaaz)
a1459.name: EU officials (anonymous
a1459.title: as relayed by Bert Wander of Avaaz)
a1459.speech: Wander said EU officials had told the campaign organisers that "they couldn't ban ivory because not enough African leaders wanted them to".

a1459.speaker: Tshekedi Khama, Botswana's environment minister
a1459.name: Tshekedi Khama
a1459.title: Botswana's environment minister
a1459.speech: "The reason the EU must close the trade is because China has closed that avenue" ; "If the EU as a bloc.. would do the right thing by doing the same, then we have two avenues out of Africa closed. If we can close the main exit areas then we are going to be a lot more succesful than we are" ; "I can't say more than say to the UK … just do the right thing, close ivory trade".

a1459.speaker: First pan-African survey of savanna elephants (2016)
a1459.name: First pan-African survey of savanna elephants (2016)
a1459.speech: According to the survey, the present elephant population is about 352,000, down from 1.3 million in 1979.

a1459.speaker: Activists
a1459.name: Activists
a1459.speech: Say the exemption for antique ivory products manufactured before 1947 creates a loophole allowing for "blood ivory" to enter the legal market.

a1535.speaker: Lord Paul Boateng, member of the House of Lords, United Kingdom
a1535.name: Lord Paul Boateng
a1535.title: member of the House of Lords, United Kingdom
a1535.speech: Urged Ghana's political leadership to take decisive action to end the nation's dependence on external aid and to combat the devaluation of local educational achievements in comparison to foreign passports: "We are held down in an impoverished and conflicted posture by our dependence on external aid and the great powers" ; "It is something terrible when a statement on the internet that a Dutch Passport is worth more than a Ghanaian PhD goes viral. We cannot allow it to be so and leadership must be at the heart of our response."

a1535.speaker: Lord Paul Boateng, member of the House of Lords, United Kingdom
a1535.name: Lord Paul Boateng
a1535.title: member of the House of Lords, United Kingdom
a1535.speech: Recalled: "Break the vicious cycle of dependence on external aid. Who here does not remember the moment His Excellency the President [Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo] stood next to the president of France [Emmanuel] Macron and went viral, making the point about the need for us to cease relying on external aid if we are to break that vicious cycle of dependence on external aid and those great powers who have fed and continue to feed on Africa's resources?"

a1535.speaker: Lord Paul Boateng, member of the House of Lords, United Kingdom
a1535.name: Lord Paul Boateng
a1535.title: member of the House of Lords, United Kingdom
a1535.speech: Addressing the theme "Fulfilling the Promise: The Challenge of Leadership! Moving from Rhetoric to Delivery," stressed that Ghana's prolonged poverty and dependence on external aid have kept the nation in a state of conflict and economic struggle; called for strong leadership to break free from this cycle and to prioritise the development and recognition of local talents and qualifications, and urged Ghana's leaders to take proactive steps to address these issues and inspire a renewed sense of pride and self-reliance among Ghanaians: "Leadership must be at the heart of our response."

a1535.speaker: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana (2018 statement, echoed)
a1535.name: Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo
a1535.title: President of Ghana (2018 statement, echoed)
a1535.speech: Emphasised, alongside French President Emmanuel Macron, Africa's need to wean itself off external aid to foster true independence and development.

a1600.speaker: Chinese officials (unnamed, at the Chinese Embassy press forum)
a1600.name: Chinese officials (unnamed
a1600.title: at the Chinese Embassy press forum)
a1600.speech: Said the sustained growth in trade illustrates not only the increased interest of Chinese companies in the Guinean market, but also the diversification of the areas of cooperation.

a1600.speaker: Huang Wei, Chinese Ambassador to Guinea
a1600.name: Huang Wei
a1600.title: Chinese Ambassador to Guinea
a1600.speech: "With regard to development aid, China has decided to cancel certain debts of Guinea and the corresponding measures have already been put in place."

a1600.speaker: Another official of the Chinese diplomatic mission in Guinea (unnamed)
a1600.name: Another official of the Chinese diplomatic mission in Guinea (unnamed)
a1600.speech: Specified that the cancelled portion of the debt amounts to 20 million yuan, or about 24.087 billion Guinean francs.

a1600.speaker: Huang Wei, Chinese Ambassador to Guinea
a1600.name: Huang Wei
a1600.title: Chinese Ambassador to Guinea
a1600.speech: Said the relevant departments of the two countries are in active consultation to deliver as soon as possible on China's promise to send a consignment of food aid to Guinea.

a1600.speaker: Huang Wei, Chinese Ambassador to Guinea
a1600.name: Huang Wei
a1600.title: Chinese Ambassador to Guinea
a1600.speech: Announcing the introduction of a 0% customs tariff for products exported to China by 33 African countries, including Guinea, indicated that "This measure aims to facilitate the export of quality Guinean products to China," while calling on Guinean economic operators to take advantage of this opportunity to boost their exports.

a1627.speaker: Edmund Yakani, civil society activist
a1627.name: Edmund Yakani
a1627.title: civil society activist
a1627.speech: Strongly condemns what he termed severe human rights violations: "I strongly condemn the violation of South Sudanese refugees, and human rights by Sudan Armed Forces during the exercise of recapturing the town of Madani from the Rapid Support Force or RSF." ; called upon the Sudanese military leadership to take responsibility: "We would like to appeal to the conflicting parties in Sudan to please don't use your politically discontented position by targeting South Sudanese refugees across several towns of Sudan." ; expressed deep concern and said targeting South Sudanese refugees is a violation of international law and that these crimes must be accounted for: "I'm calling upon the leadership of Sudan to take responsibility to ensure that as they (the Rapid Support Forces and SAF) confront themselves, they should not target South Sudanese refugees. It is a violation of international law, it is a violation of humanitarian law and this a crime that will never go and accounted for."

a1627.speaker: Sudanese authorities
a1627.name: Sudanese authorities
a1627.speech: Neither confirm nor deny those killed were South Sudanese, but said there were incidents involving individuals and that they have been arrested.

a1627.speaker: South Sudanese intellectuals in the diaspora
a1627.name: South Sudanese intellectuals in the diaspora
a1627.speech: Condemned the act on social media and called on the international community and humanitarian organizations to urgently intervene to provide protection and humanitarian assistance to South Sudanese refugees in Sudan.

a1627.speaker: Arthur Gabriel, prominent South Sudanese writer based in the U.S.
a1627.name: Arthur Gabriel
a1627.title: prominent South Sudanese writer based in the U.S.
a1627.speech: "What the Sudanese army did to the South Sudanese civilians in Madani is not new. The so-called SAF has been doing this since 1956 in South Sudan until we left. This army that we never felt represented us or belonged to."

a1627.speaker: Atem Simon, South Sudanese Senior Journalist
a1627.name: Atem Simon
a1627.title: South Sudanese Senior Journalist
a1627.speech: "I find people surprised by the actions of the Sudanese army, which they call violations. If there is another name for this army, it is the same violations."

a1627.speaker: Isam Mohamed Hassan, Sudanese Ambassador to South Sudan
a1627.name: Isam Mohamed Hassan
a1627.title: Sudanese Ambassador to South Sudan
a1627.speech: Said the social media footages have not been brought to his attention yet; however, he said there were individual incidents in Kanabi of Madani and the de facto regime issued a statement indicating the perpetrators have been arrested; he revealed that those who committed these crimes were arrested and imprisoned by the Sudan government and added that there was no directive to the forces to commit these crimes against South Sudanese: "I did not see anything on social media concerning our South Sudanese brothers in Madani, but there were incidents that occurred by some individuals in Kanabi, and a statement was issued by the government and those who committed these crimes were arrested and put on trial, but there is nothing official in directing them to do these crimes for any reason to South Sudanese brothers in Madani."

a1627.speaker: Khalid Al-Aiser, Sudanese government spokesman (official statement)
a1627.name: Khalid Al-Aiser
a1627.title: Sudanese government spokesman (official statement)
a1627.speech: "We reject any crime committed against a Sudanese man or woman anywhere in Sudan," calling on all fighters to follow the values of justice and law in dealing with prisoners suspected of collaborating with the rebellion throughout the past period.

a1659.speaker: Issaka Adamou Nourou-Dini, Director General of the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger
a1659.name: Issaka Adamou Nourou-Dini
a1659.title: Director General of the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger
a1659.speech: Said the construction of Liptako-Gourma Square falls within the framework of an urban planning respectful of our identity, in which every inhabitant can recognise themselves and feel in their place, at a time when the large cities of the sub-region are transforming rapidly to become poles of economic, cultural and tourist attraction.

a1659.speaker: Issaka Adamou Nourou-Dini, Director General of the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger
a1659.name: Issaka Adamou Nourou-Dini
a1659.title: Director General of the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger
a1659.speech: Explained that the central monument consists of a raised circular platform representing the dignity and elevation of the nations of the Confederation: "Three explanatory engravings retrace the genesis of the Authority for the Integrated Development of the Liptako-Gourma Region, the predecessor of the current Sahelo-Saharan Space. The body of the monument, symbolised by an equilateral triangle, embodies the three member countries (Burkina Faso, Niger and Mali) as well as the values of equality, justice and free movement of goods and people between these nations." ; added that at the top of the triangle a map of the three countries is held firmly by hands representing the leaders of the three nations, united in taking charge of the destiny of their peoples, and that the flags of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso surround the monument, underlining the unity and cooperation between these countries ; "The enclosure of the square, with its multiple entrances, symbolises the openness of the States of the Alliance of the Sahel towards other African nations and the whole world. The water fountain evokes the hope aroused by the current Sahelo-Saharan Space."

a1659.speaker: Issaka Adamou Nourou-Dini, Director General of the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger
a1659.name: Issaka Adamou Nourou-Dini
a1659.title: Director General of the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger
a1659.speech: Stressed that the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger (AMV-Niger) has embarked on multiple ambitious projects to modernise and beautify the country's cities, and in particular the capital: "These initiatives will soon transform our cities and provide their inhabitants with a healthy and pleasant living environment, making them a reference for many countries of the sub-region."

a1659.speaker: Issaka Adamou Nourou-Dini, Director General of the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger
a1659.name: Issaka Adamou Nourou-Dini
a1659.title: Director General of the Agency for the Modernisation of the Cities of Niger
a1659.speech: Recalled that the Liptako-Gourma region, shared between the three countries, goes well beyond a simple geographical space, embodying a common heritage forged by centuries of links between the peoples, cultures and traditions: "This region has always symbolised the natural connection between our nations, through commercial, cultural and social exchanges that transcend administrative borders."

a1777.speaker: Joint extraordinary Summit of Heads of State of SADC and the East African Community (EAC) (summit communiqué)
a1777.name: Joint extraordinary Summit of Heads of State of SADC and the East African Community (EAC) (summit communiqué)
a1777.speech: Directed that Chiefs of Defence Forces meet within 5 days and provide technical direction on immediate and unconditional ceasefire and cessation of hostilities in the Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo; further directed the Chiefs of Defence Forces to oversee the provision of humanitarian assistance including repatriation of the deceased and evacuation of the injured, to develop a securitisation plan for the intense conflict zone of Goma and its surrounding areas, to oversee the opening of main supply routes, to monitor the immediate reopening of Goma Airport and to advise on other related facilitative interventions; directed a joint meeting of EAC and SADC Ministers to be convened within 30 days to deliberate on the report of the joint meetings of SADC-EAC Chiefs of Defence Forces; agreed to merge the Luanda and Nairobi peace processes; mandated the co-chairs of the peace processes, in consultation with the African Union, to consider and appoint additional facilitators including from other regions of Africa; and directed the resumption of direct negotiations and dialogue with all state and non-state parties (military and non-military) including M23 under the framework of the merged Luanda/Nairobi Process.

a1777.speaker: SADC and EAC extraordinary Summits (29 and 31 January resolutions)
a1777.name: SADC and EAC extraordinary Summits (29 and 31 January resolutions)
a1777.speech: Both extraordinary Summits separately called for this joint summit to deliberate the way forward regarding the deteriorating security situation in the DRC, while condemning the attacks on diplomatic missions, embassies and staff based in Kinshasa; they urged the DRC to protect lives and property as well as upholding long lasting legal and moral principles of respecting peace missions in DRC such as the UN Stabilization Mission (MONUSCO) and others; and called for cessation of hostilities and an immediate ceasefire, restoration of essential utilities and supply lines for food and other essential commodities to ensure humanitarian support, and peaceful resolution of the conflict through the Luanda/Nairobi process.

a1777.speaker: SADC-EAC Heads of State
a1777.name: SADC-EAC Heads of State
a1777.speech: Reaffirmed their "solidarity and unwavering commitment to continue supporting the DRC in its pursuit of safeguarding its independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity as well as sustainable peace security and development"; similar consultations were agreed that they "shall be convened at least once every year and as, and when, the need arises to review matters of common interest to the two regions".

a1782.speaker: Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Greater Pibor
a1782.name: Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Greater Pibor
a1782.speech: Has reported that heavy floods in the Greater Pibor Administrative Area have displaced over 70,000 people, prompting local officials to issue an urgent call for international humanitarian assistance.

a1782.speaker: David Ngiro Yankon, RRC Chairperson, Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a1782.name: David Ngiro Yankon
a1782.title: RRC Chairperson, Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a1782.speech: Warned that the widespread displacement and submerging of health facilities could lead to a severe outbreak of waterborne diseases, stating that heavy rainfall and rising river levels have forced 13,907 households from their homes ; said the flood situation has been ongoing since September 7th and has affected all counties in the Greater Pibor Administrative Area, including Pibor headquarters, Gumruk, Vertet, Likwangole, and Pochalla ; “The flood has actually created a lot of damage in terms of the farmers being affected by their farms, and crops are being submerged by water” ; added that the water has also submerged air transport facilities and that many schools are no longer operational.

a1782.speaker: David Ngiro Yankon, RRC Chairperson, Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a1782.name: David Ngiro Yankon
a1782.title: RRC Chairperson, Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a1782.speech: Called on the national RRC to appeal to international humanitarian partners for support, noting that most health facilities have been shut down due to the floods: “There was also a pullout of the international organization that was operating in Gumruk and Likwangole, and also leaving these two counties in Pibor without health facilities.”

a1782.speaker: David Ngiro Yankon, RRC Chairperson, Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a1782.name: David Ngiro Yankon
a1782.title: RRC Chairperson, Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a1782.speech: Warned that the floods could lead to a health crisis: “We all know, when there is a flood like this, we expect a lot of things to happen. So, there has to be an outbreak that will come, whether it is cholera or other waterborne diseases. So, these are the things that we’re expecting to come after the flood.”

a1804.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1804.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a1804.speech: Is sounding the alarm: nearly 29 million people in six Sahel countries need humanitarian assistance and protection in 2025; according to its latest humanitarian needs overview for the region, 4.3 billion dollars are needed to assist 18.4 million people in Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Mali, Niger, Nigeria and Chad.

a1804.speaker: Charles Bernimolin, OCHA regional head for West and Central Africa
a1804.name: Charles Bernimolin
a1804.title: OCHA regional head for West and Central Africa
a1804.speech: "Millions of vulnerable women, children and men are in an emergency situation. Without adequate funding, lives will be lost." ; "These are not budget figures, but human lives. Inaction will be costly," he warned, calling for an urgent mobilisation of donors.

a1817.speaker: Some protesters in Boston (anonymous)
a1817.name: Some protesters in Boston (anonymous)
a1817.speech: Told the BBC that they were motivated by immigration raids on US university students that have led to arrests and deportation proceedings.

a1817.speaker: BBC (report)
a1817.name: BBC (report)
a1817.speech: "Law student Katie Smith told BBC News that she was motivated by Turkish international student Rumeysa Ozturk, whose arrest near Boston-area Tufts University by masked US agents was caught on camera last month."

a1817.speaker: Protest organisers
a1817.name: Protest organisers
a1817.speech: Said they have three demands, CNN reported. They want "an end to the billionaire takeover and rampant corruption of the Trump administration; an end to slashing federal funds for Medicaid, Social Security, and other programs working people rely on; and an end to the attacks on immigrants, trans people, and other communities." ; Described Saturday's protest as a success attended by millions of people in several countries.

a1817.speaker: Protesters in London
a1817.name: Protesters in London
a1817.speech: Chanted, "Hands off Canada", "Hands off Greenland" and "Hands off Ukraine," in response to Mr Trump's proposals to annex Canada and Greenland and essentially get Ukraine to surrender to Russia.

a1817.speaker: Democratic lawmakers in Washington DC
a1817.name: Democratic lawmakers in Washington DC
a1817.speech: Addressed protesters, telling the crowd that the Trump administration had been taken over by billionaires.

a1817.speaker: Maxwell Frost, Florida Congressman
a1817.name: Maxwell Frost
a1817.title: Florida Congressman
a1817.speech: Denounced the "billionaire takeover of our government" ; "When you steal from the people, expect the people to rise up. At the ballot box and in the streets."

a1817.speaker: Rahna Epting, Executive Director, MoveOn
a1817.name: Rahna Epting
a1817.title: Executive Director, MoveOn
a1817.speech: "What we witnessed today was nothing short of extraordinary. Across the country and around the world, people came together to say: we will not be silent while our rights, our futures, and our democracy are under attack. This peaceful movement is powered by everyday people—nurses, teachers, students, parents—who are rising up to protect what matters most. We are united, we are relentless, and we are just getting started."

a1911.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Türkiye
a1911.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
a1911.title: President of Türkiye
a1911.speech: Hailed the bilateral relationship, now elevated to the level of a High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council, and said talks with Sonko covered key sectors including investment, trade, security, defense, counter-terrorism, energy, mining, transportation, agriculture, and fisheries ; expressed a joint ambition to raise bilateral trade to $1 billion, noting that nearly 100 Turkish companies operate in Senegal, with total investments and projects valued at around $3 billion ; reaffirmed Türkiye's commitment to supporting Senegal's Vision 2050 national transformation program.

a1911.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Türkiye
a1911.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
a1911.title: President of Türkiye
a1911.speech: Praised Senegal's stance on international affairs, especially regarding Palestine, thanking Dakar for its support of Turkish initiatives at the United Nations ; recalled Senegal's long-standing role since 1975 as chair of the UN Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People, and denounced the ongoing situation in Gaza as "genocide," vowing to continue advocating until those responsible are held accountable.

a1911.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Türkiye
a1911.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
a1911.title: President of Türkiye
a1911.speech: Thanked Senegalese authorities for their support in combating the FETÖ organisation, describing Africa as the continent of the future, and stating that no globally ambitious country can afford to "turn its back on the region."

a1911.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.name: Ousmane Sonko
a1911.title: Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.speech: Delivering remarks at the ceremony, conveyed greetings from President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and emphasised the strategic importance of this visit ; lauded Türkiye as a model of economic success and reiterated his government's commitment to addressing inherited challenges, particularly in budget management ; "You have always stood by us – a true big brother. Türkiye is now a global model of success," welcoming Türkiye's ambition to triple trade with Senegal ; pledged that Dakar would mobilise all necessary efforts to achieve that goal within a framework of mutually beneficial partnership.

a1911.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.name: Ousmane Sonko
a1911.title: Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.speech: Stressed the need for balanced, respectful cooperation, adding that Senegal intends to develop without relying on foreign aid, and seeks to establish a new model of win-win agreements.

a1911.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.name: Ousmane Sonko
a1911.title: Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.speech: On regional security, pointed to rising threats facing Senegal and called for greater military sovereignty and domestic security capacity amid instability in neighboring countries ; praised the strength of Türkiye's defense industry and expressed confidence in the partnership's ability to equip Senegalese forces effectively.

a1911.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.name: Ousmane Sonko
a1911.title: Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.speech: On the Gaza crisis, denounced the situation as a "planned genocide" and criticised the inaction of major powers in the face of Palestinian suffering, especially among children ; reaffirmed Senegal's commitment within UN bodies and saluted Erdoğan's firm stance: "You are one of the few leaders standing up against this genocide."

a1911.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.name: Ousmane Sonko
a1911.title: Prime Minister of Senegal
a1911.speech: Announced his participation in the upcoming Türkiye–Senegal Economic Forum in Istanbul, and called for expanded economic ties, particularly in transportation, energy, and local resource mobilization ; "In this transitional phase, we need your support more than ever," reaffirming confidence in the Turkish development model and advocating for deeper bilateral ties rooted in sovereignty, dignity, and mutual respect.

a1951.speaker: Ukraine and its European allies
a1951.name: Ukraine and its European allies
a1951.speech: Are proposing to Russia a complete and unconditional ceasefire for at least 30 days starting Monday, with the aim of creating an environment conducive to peace negotiations; the proposal was presented during a meeting in Kyiv between the Ukrainian president and the leaders of France, Germany, the United Kingdom and Poland.

a1951.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
a1951.name: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
a1951.speech: Stated that the truce could “open the way to peace negotiations”.

a1951.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a1951.name: Donald Trump
a1951.title: President of the United States
a1951.speech: Expressed support for the proposal and showed willingness to pressure Moscow through new sanctions should Russia reject the truce.

a1951.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a1951.name: Emmanuel Macron
a1951.title: President of France
a1951.speech: Stressed that a lasting peace requires a complete and unconditional ceasefire and criticised Russia for imposing conditions aimed at buying time.

a1951.speaker: The Kremlin
a1951.name: The Kremlin
a1951.speech: Has so far not responded officially to the proposal.

a1951.speaker: Dmitri Peskov, spokesman for the Russian government
a1951.name: Dmitri Peskov
a1951.title: spokesman for the Russian government
a1951.speech: Said that Russia will not let itself be intimidated by threats of sanctions and that any truce must take into account the realities on the ground.

a2022.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia
a2022.name: Vladimir Putin
a2022.title: President of Russia
a2022.speech: According to President Putin, strengthening ties with African countries is one of the priorities of Russia's foreign policy. ; In an interview granted to the Russian news agency TASS before the summit, the Russian head of state declared that "Russian-African relations are on the rise" and spoke of offers in the areas of political and diplomatic support, defence and security assistance, economic assistance, humanitarian aid and education.

a2301.speaker: Tammy Bruce, spokesperson for the US State Department (statement)
a2301.name: Tammy Bruce
a2301.title: spokesperson for the US State Department (statement)
a2301.speech: "Pursuant to the Executive Order of the Presidency concerning the re-evaluation and realignment of United States foreign aid, Secretary Rubio has suspended all US foreign aid financed by, or through, the State Department and USAID, for the purposes of re-evaluation." ; According to the spokesperson, the aim of the measure is to ensure that foreign aid programmes are efficient and aligned with US international policy, in keeping with the agenda known as "America First." ; "The President has made it clear that the United States will no longer hand out money blindly, with no return for the American people. Re-evaluating and realigning foreign aid for the benefit of hard-working taxpayers is not only the right thing to do, it is a moral imperative." ; "The mandate that came from the American people was clear - we need to focus on American national interests. The Department and USAID take their role as stewards of taxpayer dollars very seriously. The implementation of this Executive Order and of the Secretary's directive advances that mission."

a2301.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a2301.name: Marco Rubio
a2301.title: US Secretary of State
a2301.speech: underlined the need for rigour in the use of foreign aid funds, emphasising that every initiative must meet three fundamental criteria: "Every dollar we spend, every programme we fund and every policy we seek to promote must be justified by the answer to three simple questions: Does it make the United States safer? Does it make the United States stronger? Does it make the United States more prosperous?"

a2301.speaker: US State Department memorandum
a2301.name: US State Department memorandum
a2301.speech: mentions specific exemptions, such as military financing for Israel and Egypt, as well as emergency food assistance.

a2301.speaker: Kyeh Kim, vice-president of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2301.name: Kyeh Kim
a2301.title: vice-president of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2301.speech: said last October that the third MCC compact aims to promote strategic investments in sectors such as land, air, maritime, digital and human connectivity and mobility, and is due to be signed in April 2026.

a2301.speaker: New York Times (citing sources connected to the programme)
a2301.name: New York Times (citing sources connected to the programme)
a2301.speech: reveals that there are now patients whose treatments have been interrupted and whose appointments have been cancelled, following the suspension of the distribution of HIV medicines under PEPFAR.

a2301.speaker: Committee for the Coordination of the Fight Against AIDS (CCS-SIDA), Cabo Verde
a2301.name: Committee for the Coordination of the Fight Against AIDS (CCS-SIDA)
a2301.title: Cabo Verde
a2301.speech: clarified to Expresso das Ilhas that it does not receive financing from the United States of America; according to the institution, its resources come from Switzerland and are already available in the country, thereby guaranteeing the continuity of the programmes supporting people living with HIV and the pregnant women with whom they work. CCS-SIDA further stressed that it has no link whatsoever with the World Bank, its main funder being the Global Fund.

a2301.speaker: Euridice Mascarenhas, president of the National Commission for Human Rights and Citizenship (CNDHC)
a2301.name: Euridice Mascarenhas
a2301.title: president of the National Commission for Human Rights and Citizenship (CNDHC)
a2301.speech: confirmed that the institution does not currently run programmes financed by the USA, although it has had American support in the past.

a2430.speaker: Jacob Aligo, Central Equatoria State Minister of Peacebuilding and Acting Minister of Information
a2430.name: Jacob Aligo
a2430.title: Central Equatoria State Minister of Peacebuilding and Acting Minister of Information
a2430.speech: Revealed, following the first cabinet meeting chaired by newly appointed Governor Rabi Mujung in Juba, that anti-corruption efforts are among the top priorities of Governor Mujung’s administration, alongside peacebuilding and inclusive development ; “On top of these priorities are peace, security, and unity in Central Equatoria State. His Excellency the Governor outlined the government’s commitment to addressing peace and stability, and promoting unity among the people and institutions in the state.” ; said the Governor also stressed the need for improved service delivery across all government institutions, urging them to redouble efforts in serving the public effectively.

a2430.speaker: Rabi Mujung, newly appointed Governor of Central Equatoria State
a2430.name: Rabi Mujung
a2430.title: newly appointed Governor of Central Equatoria State
a2430.speech: Has vowed not to entertain any form of corruption in his administration after chairing his first cabinet meeting on Thursday ; reiterated his readiness to work with all stakeholders and investors to drive socio-economic development and to support entrepreneurs so they can contribute positively to the state’s economic recovery ; emphasised the importance of transparency and accountability as foundational principles of good governance ; pledged to support the State Relief and Rehabilitation Commission in strengthening disaster preparedness, emergency response, and the provision of humanitarian assistance.

a2434.speaker: Bank of Botswana (BoB) Quarterly Business Expectations Survey, March 2025
a2434.name: Bank of Botswana (BoB) Quarterly Business Expectations Survey
a2434.title: March 2025
a2434.speech: Indicates that while companies remain hopeful about business conditions, the sentiment is slightly less upbeat compared to the fourth quarter of 2024; industries such as Retail, Accommodation, Transport, Communications, Manufacturing, Mining and Quarrying are leading the optimism, while Agriculture remains neutral and Finance, Professional and Administrative Activities, and Construction and Real Estate express a more pessimistic outlook ; “The business environment is showing signs of gradual improvement, but the sentiment is not as strong as it was in the previous quarter. Despite this, firms expect favourable conditions, particularly in the first and second quarters of the year.”

a2434.speaker: Bank of Botswana (BoB) Quarterly Business Expectations Survey, March 2025
a2434.name: Bank of Botswana (BoB) Quarterly Business Expectations Survey
a2434.title: March 2025
a2434.speech: Reports that firms predict a decrease in cost pressures in early 2025, driven mainly by a reduction in input costs, in line with expectations that inflation will remain within BoB’s objective range of 3 to 6 percent; that companies expect an increase in both lending interest rates and borrowing volumes by March 2026; and forecasts a modest economic rebound in 2025, with overall output expected to grow by 1.9 percent, a recovery from the 3 percent contraction recorded in 2024.

a2434.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Botswana
a2434.name: Ministry of Finance of Botswana
a2434.speech: Forecast 3.3 percent growth, above the survey’s 1.9 percent projection.

a2434.speaker: Bank of Botswana (BoB) Quarterly Business Expectations Survey, March 2025
a2434.name: Bank of Botswana (BoB) Quarterly Business Expectations Survey
a2434.title: March 2025
a2434.speech: “While businesses face challenges, particularly from exchange rate fluctuations and the availability of raw materials, supportive factors such as political stability, reliable electricity, and a favourable regulatory environment continue to bolster confidence” ; “The business community appears to be cautiously optimistic about the coming year, balancing potential risks with strategic opportunities.”

a2436.speaker: Joseph Chewe, President of the Mine Workers Union of Zambia (MUZ)
a2436.name: Joseph Chewe
a2436.title: President of the Mine Workers Union of Zambia (MUZ)
a2436.speech: Has said any responsible and patriotic Zambian must support the agenda of forming a federation of mine workers’ unions to protect and safeguard the interests of mine workers and also ensure that mineral resources in Africa benefit the respective countries and people; said MUZ and the General Union of Workers in Mines and Quarries and the Navigations (GUWMQN) of Egypt were in the process of forming such a federation; said the initiative would see mine workers’ interests protected as well as mineral resources through adding value to them as opposed to exporting raw materials to other countries ; “We have therefore partnered with an Egyptian mine union counterpart where they are seeking to form a federation of mine unions to advance the interests of workers and protect minerals in the two countries as well as across the African continent. We are set to form a federation of mine unions with our Egyptian mine union counterparts called the African Federation of mine workers unions aimed at protecting the interests of workers and minerals across the two countries and the African continent.” ; said the federation, which would be open to all African mining countries, intends to tap into the African Union (AU) and International Labour Organisation (ILO) among others towards using the continent’s mineral resources to provide job creation and alleviate poverty ; said last week that MUZ was undergoing transformation and so it was imperative that it created networks with other mine unions in other countries to learn how they were operating to advance the interests of workers and minerals in order to foster national development in Zambia.

a2436.speaker: Joseph Chewe, President of the Mine Workers Union of Zambia (MUZ)
a2436.name: Joseph Chewe
a2436.title: President of the Mine Workers Union of Zambia (MUZ)
a2436.speech: Asked how the federation would achieve its goals when some African leaders were puppets and stooges of imperialists, said achieving the goals and objectives must not be left to the federation alone, but to all responsible and patriotic Zambians: “This issue is not about MUZ and GUWMQN only, but all patriotic and responsible Zambians, in particular, and Africans in general who want to see that mineral resources in Africa benefit Africans. So, I am calling on you, the media and other Zambians in general, to support this agenda.”

a2436.speaker: Mohammed Samara, President of the General Union of Workers in Mines and Quarries and the Navigations (GUWMQN) of Egypt
a2436.name: Mohammed Samara
a2436.title: President of the General Union of Workers in Mines and Quarries and the Navigations (GUWMQN) of Egypt
a2436.speech: Said the federation would soon establish structures across Africa in order to improve the living standards of the worker: “In order for the mining sector to be revamped, it is important that its workforce is taken care of. This federation we want to get into with our mine union counterpart in Zambia will help in advocating for the interests of miners and also the mineral resources for both countries and Africa as a whole. So, we will work together to ensure the mining sector in Zambia and Egypt thrives.”

a2469.speaker: European Union, United States and seven other foreign missions in Malawi (joint statement)
a2469.name: European Union
a2469.title: United States and seven other foreign missions in Malawi (joint statement)
a2469.speech: Have strongly condemned Thursday's machete attacks on protesters in Lilongwe, warning that the violence—in full view of security forces—threatens the integrity and credibility of the September 16 General Election ; In a joint statement issued yesterday, the heads of mission expressed alarm over "a trend of violence during peaceful and lawful demonstrations in Malawi's cities" ; They stated that the right to freedom of assembly is enshrined in the Malawi Constitution and must be protected.

a2469.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2469.name: Rune Skinnebach
a2469.title: EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2469.speech: Said the incident raises serious concerns about the credibility and safety of the electoral process: "This, for me, is of huge concern. We are not even in the formal campaign period yet, and incidents like these, where police appear unwilling or unable to perform their role, are a huge concern." ; The envoy also questioned the political logic behind the attack, arguing it could backfire against those who orchestrated it: "I don't know what to think of this, because I find it so unstrategic. Whoever deployed those guys with pangas—and I'm sure it was orchestrated from somewhere—made a huge mistake. I don't think Malawians want violence in their elections. I don't think Malawians want people chasing them with pangas when they exercise their right to express their views.
