I don't think that you gain support as a political party by being suspected of mobilising such types."

a2469.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2469.name: Rune Skinnebach
a2469.title: EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2469.speech: While reaffirming the EU's readiness to observe the elections, Skinnebach said the observer mission's deployment depends on swift administrative steps and a secure environment: "The EU has accepted Malawi's invitation to observe the election, but is awaiting final paperwork."

a2469.speaker: Amy Diaz, US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires (statement)
a2469.name: Amy Diaz
a2469.title: US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires (statement)
a2469.speech: The US Embassy issued a parallel condemnation in which Chargé d'Affaires Amy Diaz said she was "sickened" by the scenes of violence, particularly the apparent inaction of State security personnel ; "What was particularly appalling was the failure of the Malawi Police Service and Malawi Defence Force to carry out their duties to protect their fellow citizens. A fundamental duty of government is to ensure that citizens can freely exercise their rights under the Constitution."

a2469.speaker: Malawi Law Society (MLS) (statement)
a2469.name: Malawi Law Society (MLS) (statement)
a2469.speech: In a strongly worded statement, the MLS accused the State of deliberately suppressing constitutional freedoms, citing Sections 15 and 38 of the Malawi Constitution to support its position ; MLS added that Thursday's events raised serious doubts about the Police Inspector General (IG) Merlyne Yolamu's "competence and impartiality" ; The law society has since demanded decisive action, including the dismissal of senior government officials, Minister of Homeland Security Ezekiel Ching'oma and Yolamu.

a2469.speaker: Media Institute of Southern Africa–Malawi Chapter (Misa-Malawi) (statement signed by chairperson Golden Matonga)
a2469.name: Media Institute of Southern Africa–Malawi Chapter (Misa-Malawi) (statement signed by chairperson Golden Matonga)
a2469.speech: Expressed deep concern over the State's failure to protect both protesters and journalists from politically motivated violence: "The State's deliberate procrastination and impunity on panga-wielding groups attacking protesters is not only appalling but contravenes the Republican Constitution, which guarantees the right to assembly and emphasises the State's obligation in protecting its citizens."

a2469.speaker: Merlyne Yolamu, Police Inspector General (Malawi)
a2469.name: Merlyne Yolamu
a2469.title: Police Inspector General (Malawi)
a2469.speech: Yolamu promised the nation during the Public Affairs Committee all-inclusive conference in Blantyre, the police would maintain peace and discharge its duties without fear or favour.

a2469.speaker: Malawi Peace and Unity Commission (MPUC) (statement signed by chairperson Mary Nkosi)
a2469.name: Malawi Peace and Unity Commission (MPUC) (statement signed by chairperson Mary Nkosi)
a2469.speech: Has called upon the police and all relevant authorities to promptly investigate the incident, identify and prosecute those responsible, and implement measures to prevent future violence ; "Continued inaction erodes public confidence in law enforcement institutions and poses a serious threat to national unity."

a2469.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) (statement)
a2469.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) (statement)
a2469.speech: Described "the vicious assault on unarmed citizens to the burning of their vehicles" as a grave violation of human rights and a blatant attack on Malawi's democratic fabric ; "If the so-called 'panga team' had been affiliated with the opposition, we are convinced that arrests would have been swift and ruthless. The continued failure to bring these assailants to justice points directly to political protection from the highest levels of power in the governing party. We will not normalize lawlessness nor will we be intimidated into silence. The failure of the MPS to uphold law and order in this matter is a dangerous signal to the nation that justice is no longer blind, but selectively applied", warning the police's credibility "is hanging by a thread".

a2469.speaker: Public Affairs Committee (PAC) (statement)
a2469.name: Public Affairs Committee (PAC) (statement)
a2469.speech: PAC said while it respected the police and MDF for the tireless job they discharge in the country, the act of negligence had gone too far to swallow ; "We call upon the MPS to uphold their pledge of professionalism as pronounced during the 6th All-Inclusive Stakeholders Conference held in May 2025… As we move towards elections, let us stand for peace, justice, and the rule of law."

a2469.speaker: Victor Chipofya Jnr, political analyst
a2469.name: Victor Chipofya Jnr
a2469.title: political analyst
a2469.speech: Observed the incident has the potential to plunge the country into a civil unrest which would be disastrous for the country. He also agreed with calls for Yolamu and Ching'oma to resign "unless they give a proper explanation why they did not act and witnessed citizens being beaten" ; "What happened is retrogressive. Instead of moving forward we are moving backwards. That could plunge the country into anarchy and that will destroy our nation. Many countries have plunged into civil wars because of such incidents."

a2469.speaker: Benedicto Kondowe, Civil Society Elections Integrity Forum (CSEIF) chairman
a2469.name: Benedicto Kondowe
a2469.title: Civil Society Elections Integrity Forum (CSEIF) chairman
a2469.speech: Said the calls for the two officials' removal were legitimate demands for accountability and not emotional reactions: "When those tasked with protecting rights instead enable or overlook their violation, they must answer for it. Failure to act only normalizes impunity. Their resignation or removal is essential to restore public trust, uphold the rule of law, and affirm that no public office is above responsibility."

a2469.speaker: Benedicto Kondowe, Civil Society Elections Integrity Forum (CSEIF) chairman
a2469.name: Benedicto Kondowe
a2469.title: Civil Society Elections Integrity Forum (CSEIF) chairman
a2469.speech: Kondowe said Malawi was treading a dangerous path as suppressing dissent weakens the country's democracy and emboldens abuse: "If leaders continue to neglect their duty while citizens are brutalized, fear will replace freedom, and silence will masquerade as peace. This leads to growing public unrest, loss of institutional credibility, and democratic decay. Bold action is needed now to steer the country back to constitutional order."

a2469.speaker: Master Dicks Mfune, expert in conflict and peace management
a2469.name: Master Dicks Mfune
a2469.title: expert in conflict and peace management
a2469.speech: Observed the removal of the two public officers was not a solution as the issue is about the legacy of political violence: "This is a legacy of political violence that has been passed on so even if they fire the two, the system will not be broken. So this is likely to escalate as we move closer to the elections and I am seeing more demonstrations and violent acts after the elections… The major implication is that people and other stakeholders may not accept the outcome of the elections."

a2469.speaker: Shadrec Namalomba, Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) spokesperson
a2469.name: Shadrec Namalomba
a2469.title: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) spokesperson
a2469.speech: The opposition DPP has said leaders of all opposition parties were meeting on the incident: "This is a sad day for Malawi. The genocide in Rwanda began with young men wielding pangas and brutally attacking their own countrymen, while government. It is a tragic reality that such atrocities are now a common occurrence here in Malawi. Despite having a President Lazarus Chakwera, who has the power to condemn and arrest these criminals, has chosen to turn a blind eye." ; However, he said while demands to have the minister and police head removed or resign were justifiable, they were not enough.

a2545.speaker: Coscel-CI (Framework for Consultation of Civil Society for Elections in Cote d'Ivoire) (findings/previous communiques)
a2545.name: Coscel-CI (Framework for Consultation of Civil Society for Elections in Cote d'Ivoire) (findings/previous communiques)
a2545.speech: Its results confirm Coscel-CI's previous communiques on the 2024 electoral roll revision, which pointed to several major challenges affecting the process: notably low participation by the population, largely due to a lack of information, to indirect costs linked to obtaining certain necessary administrative documents and to delays in their delivery; technical problems, notably malfunctions of the biometric tablets, which considerably slowed enrolment operations; and the inconsistent application of the rules in certain centres, which hampered the fluidity of the process.

a2545.speaker: Coscel-CI (Framework for Consultation of Civil Society for Elections in Cote d'Ivoire) (recommendations)
a2545.name: Coscel-CI (Framework for Consultation of Civil Society for Elections in Cote d'Ivoire) (recommendations)
a2545.speech: Faced with all these challenges, Coscel-CI recommends strengthening communication and raising public awareness about the free-of-charge nature of the necessary administrative documents and about the location of enrolment centres; ensuring the proper functioning of equipment, notably the biometric tablets, before their deployment; and extending the enrolment period to allow broader coverage and increased participation by the population.

a2578.speaker: Peter Mutharika, Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) president and former Malawi leader
a2578.name: Peter Mutharika
a2578.title: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) president and former Malawi leader
a2578.speech: slammed the government for its failure to address the rising cost of living, saying families can no longer afford basic necessities like maize and soap: "Families can no longer afford essentials like maize and soap. Businesses are struggling to import goods due to foreign exchange challenges, and small businesses are shutting down. Young people are losing hope, and families are being torn apart by poverty."

a2578.speaker: Peter Mutharika, Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) president and former Malawi leader
a2578.name: Peter Mutharika
a2578.title: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) president and former Malawi leader
a2578.speech: highlighted how skyrocketing fertilizer prices and the failures of the Affordable Inputs Programme (AIP) have exacerbated hunger in the country: "The AIP, once hailed as a game-changer, has become a national disgrace. Corruption and inefficiency have humiliated the nation."

a2578.speaker: Peter Mutharika, Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) president and former Malawi leader
a2578.name: Peter Mutharika
a2578.title: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) president and former Malawi leader
a2578.speech: accused the current administration of fostering oppression, saying Malawi has become a "police state" where political opponents and critics live in fear of persecution: "Fuel shortages will not end through oppression, hunger will not be eradicated through political witch-hunts, and medicines will not return to hospitals by silencing your critics."

a2578.speaker: Peter Mutharika, Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) president and former Malawi leader
a2578.name: Peter Mutharika
a2578.title: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) president and former Malawi leader
a2578.speech: contrasted the current state of the nation with his time in office, claiming his administration prioritized economic stability and affordable living for Malawians. He said his party has already developed policies to revive the economy, support farmers, and improve livelihoods.

a2578.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2578.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2578.title: President of Malawi
a2578.speech: in a recent address, said his government is mobilizing resources to mitigate hunger and has committed to addressing the challenges facing Malawians.

a2875.speaker: Africa CDC (African Union health agency)
a2875.name: Africa CDC (African Union health agency)
a2875.speech: Affirmed on Thursday that US President Donald Trump's decision to withdraw the United States from the World Health Organization (WHO) would have a significant impact on public health programmes in Africa.

a2875.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2875.name: Donald Trump
a2875.title: US President
a2875.speech: Signed the executive order a few hours after his inauguration on Monday, justifying this withdrawal by the gap between American and Chinese financial contributions.

a2875.speaker: Ngashi Ngongo, chief of staff of Africa CDC
a2875.name: Ngashi Ngongo
a2875.title: chief of staff of Africa CDC
a2875.speech: Affirmed that it was "a decision of high importance for Africa." The United States "are one of the main contributors to public health in Africa", he declared during an online press briefing ; specified that Africa CDC itself does not "really expect that much impact" from the American withdrawal, if it is confirmed, less than 10% of its funding currently coming from the United States. On the other hand, this withdrawal would "greatly" affect the agency's member states, he said, stressing that many African countries receive funds in particular from the American PEPFAR programme to fight AIDS.

a2875.speaker: Ngashi Ngongo, chief of staff of Africa CDC
a2875.name: Ngashi Ngongo
a2875.title: chief of staff of Africa CDC
a2875.speech: Asked whether China or other countries could fill the shortfall, said that Africa CDC would have to be open to "well-intentioned countries that can come to the rescue of African member states."

a2875.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) and the African Union (AU)
a2875.name: World Health Organization (WHO) and the African Union (AU)
a2875.speech: Both deplored this decision, calling on the United States to reconsider it.

a2875.speaker: African Union (AU)
a2875.name: African Union (AU)
a2875.speech: Warned on Wednesday: "The United States were one of the first and strong supporters of the creation of Africa CDC", which works with the WHO to "detect, prepare for, respond to and recover from pandemics."

a2876.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a2876.name: Daniel Chapo
a2876.title: President of Mozambique
a2876.speech: According to President Daniel Chapo, the province of Zambezia needs 1.5 billion meticais (about 23 million US dollars) to repair the damage caused by the post-election rioting ; said that among the buildings attacked by rioters were schools, health units and the police commands in Morrumbala, Namacurra and Mocubela districts ; he said he had visited several Zambezia districts "because of the violent, illegal and criminal demonstrations. There were huge losses in Zambezia calculated at 1.5 billion meticais".

a2876.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a2876.name: Daniel Chapo
a2876.title: President of Mozambique
a2876.speech: "We cannot destroy our own house", declared Chapo, "because tomorrow we may need the things that we are now destroying. People destroyed petrol pumps, and they woke up the following day to find that there was nowhere where they could refuel their cars" ; he claimed that the same people who had vandalised commercial infrastructures then tried to organise other demonstrations against food and fuel shortages and price rises which resulted precisely from the rioting they had stoked.

a2876.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a2876.name: Daniel Chapo
a2876.title: President of Mozambique
a2876.speech: Said the government is determined to carry out "structuring projects" in Zambezia, such as a bridge over the Licungo river in Mocuba district, and a network of roads between the districts of the province ; "We are taking the decision that next year, come rain, come shine, with or without the MCA, we shall build the bridge and the roads", declared Chapo.

a2876.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a2876.name: Daniel Chapo
a2876.title: President of Mozambique
a2876.speech: He was also confident that the project to build a new deep water port at Macuse will go ahead, and provide a large number of jobs for young people in Zambezia ; added that the government is in discussions with the publicly owned rail and port company to transform the port of Quelimane into a reference port for developing the province ; he also promised to bring industry back to Zambezia.

a3010.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB source)
a3010.name: African Development Bank (AfDB source)
a3010.speech: Said the African Development Bank has contributed $1 million from its Special Relief Fund to provide emergency food assistance to flood-affected communities in northeastern Nigeria.

a3010.speaker: David Stevenson, WFP's Country Director in Nigeria
a3010.name: David Stevenson
a3010.title: WFP's Country Director in Nigeria
a3010.speech: “The African Development Bank’s support is timely and comes as a lifeline for those struggling to feed themselves amidst rising food prices and economic turmoil” ; “Communities which, after years of conflict and violence, started rebuilding their lives were struck by the floods and once again displaced, meaning more and more people cannot support themselves and their families.”

a3010.speaker: Cadre Harmonisé food security analysis (November 2024, 26 states and the federal capital)
a3010.name: Cadre Harmonisé food security analysis (November 2024
a3010.title: 26 states and the federal capital)
a3010.speech: Projects that 33 million people in Nigeria will face food insecurity by August 2025.

a3010.speaker: Abdul Kamara, African Development Bank Director General in Nigeria
a3010.name: Abdul Kamara
a3010.title: African Development Bank Director General in Nigeria
a3010.speech: “I hope that this additional funding will mitigate the suffering of vulnerable people on the brink of acute hunger at a time when more Nigerians than ever need humanitarian assistance” ; “I commend the Federal Government of Nigeria and WFP for the continuous efforts to operate in such a challenging environment to improve the lives of Nigerian families.”

a3130.speaker: Government of Lesotho
a3130.name: Government of Lesotho
a3130.speech: says it is shocked by US President Donald Trump saying that “nobody has ever heard of” the southern African nation.

a3130.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3130.name: Donald Trump
a3130.title: US President
a3130.speech: “Eight million dollars to promote LGBTQI+ in the African nation of Lesotho, which nobody has ever heard of,” Trump said, made while addressing the US Congress as he listed cuts to what he said was wasteful expenditure.

a3130.speaker: Spokesperson for Lesotho’s foreign affairs department (unnamed)
a3130.name: Spokesperson for Lesotho’s foreign affairs department (unnamed)
a3130.speech: told the BBC that Lesotho enjoyed “warm and cordial” relations with the US.

a3130.speaker: US government
a3130.name: US government
a3130.speech: According to the US government, the two countries traded goods worth $240m (£187m) in 2024, mostly exports from Lesotho to the US, in particular textiles and clothing.

a3130.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho’s Foreign Affairs Minister
a3130.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a3130.title: Lesotho’s Foreign Affairs Minister
a3130.speech: said it was “shocking” to hear a head of state “refer to another sovereign state in that manner” ; “To my surprise, ‘the country that nobody has heard of’ is the country where the US has a permanent mission” ; “Lesotho is a member of the UN and of a number of other international bodies. And the US has an embassy here and [there are] a number of US organisations we’ve accommodated here in Maseru.”

a3130.speaker: Lesotho officials (unnamed)
a3130.name: Lesotho officials (unnamed)
a3130.speech: dismissed Trump’s remarks as “off the cuff” and a “political statement”, adding that they were “uncalled-for” given the good relations between the two nations.

a3130.speaker: Kutloano Pheko, Lesotho foreign affairs spokesperson
a3130.name: Kutloano Pheko
a3130.title: Lesotho foreign affairs spokesperson
a3130.speech: “We maintain very warm and cordial relations with the US. They’ve got a mission in Maseru and we also have [one] in Washington,” Mr Pheko told the BBC ; was unable to confirm Trump’s comments on the funding that went to LGBTQ organisations, saying that as the money went directly to them, they would be best placed to comment.

a3130.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho’s Foreign Affairs Minister
a3130.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a3130.title: Lesotho’s Foreign Affairs Minister
a3130.speech: confirmed that the country had been affected by Trump’s sudden decision to pause aid funding to countries around the world, but declined to criticise this decision, saying it was the US’s “prerogative to cut aid if they want to”.

a3130.speaker: Lesotho health ministry
a3130.name: Lesotho health ministry
a3130.speech: told South African publication GroundUp in February that Lesotho is among those countries that benefited from Pepfar, with TB and HIV programmes among those receiving the critical funds.

a3162.speaker: Dr. Qu Dongyu, FAO Director-General
a3162.name: Dr. Qu Dongyu
a3162.title: FAO Director-General
a3162.speech: noted that the countries most impacted by food insecurity are often those with the least access to finance ; warned that without strategic interventions, these nations will continue to face devastating consequences, trapped in cycles of poverty, low productivity, and food shortages.

a3162.speaker: Dr. Qu Dongyu, FAO Director-General
a3162.name: Dr. Qu Dongyu
a3162.title: FAO Director-General
a3162.speech: "Scaling up for food security and rural development is essential. This involves not only mobilising resources but also identifying strategic investment opportunities that can have far-reaching impacts. The FAO Hand-in-Hand Initiative and its Investment Forum, under the umbrella of the World Food Forum, exemplifies this approach." ; "To solve the lack of access to finance, countries must rely on timely and solid information - data, science, and evidence - to pinpoint needs and develop effective solutions" ; added that FAO's Geospatial Platform and analytical tools were instrumental in shaping the strategic visions and actions needed to address food security challenges.

a3162.speaker: The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) report, 2024 edition
a3162.name: The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) report
a3162.title: 2024 edition
a3162.speech: findings cited that the countries most impacted by food insecurity are often those with the least access to finance.

a3162.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) report
a3162.name: World Food Programme (WFP) report
a3162.speech: reported that nearly one third of Lesotho's population is experiencing acute food insecurity and requires urgent humanitarian assistance; the report underlines that many households in Lesotho are particularly vulnerable, lacking the resilience to recover from economic shocks, with neither savings nor access to credit.

a3162.speaker: King Letsie III of Lesotho
a3162.name: King Letsie III of Lesotho
a3162.speech: addressed the profound inequalities in access to food worldwide, saying the theme, "Right to Foods for a Better Life and a Better Future," is not just a vision but a call to action: "It is a commitment to building a healthier and more equitable tomorrow for all," urging nations to view access to food as a fundamental human right rather than a privilege ; underscored the alarming statistic that, in 2023, one in 11 people globally, and one in five in Africa, faced hunger ; "The right to food goes beyond merely addressing hunger, it is about ensuring everyone has access to diverse, nutritious foods that contribute to a healthy and dignified life" ; lamented that a third of the world's population cannot afford a healthy diet, which not only exacerbates hunger but also contributes to the growing epidemic of malnutrition, being overweight, and obesity.

a3162.speaker: King Letsie III of Lesotho
a3162.name: King Letsie III of Lesotho
a3162.speech: expressed optimism, noting that the power to reverse these trends lies within collective efforts to transform agrifood systems: "Achieving good nutrition is not just an aspiration, it is an achievable goal that we must strive for collectively" ; called on governments, organisations, and communities to prioritise investments in sustainable agricultural practices that ensure access to healthy diets for all people, regardless of their economic status.

a3381.speaker: Sussex.com (Harry and Meghan’s new website)
a3381.name: Sussex.com (Harry and Meghan’s new website)
a3381.speech: “Prince Harry has long advocated for the power of sport for healing and building community. He was honoured to present this award and highlight the importance of giving back.”

a3381.speaker: Sussexroyal.com (website message)
a3381.name: Sussexroyal.com (website message)
a3381.speech: A message pops up redirecting users to the new site: “This site was established in 2020 and sets out the work streams of Prince Harry and Meghan, The Duke and Duchess of Sussex prior to their move to the United States. To learn more about the royal couple and their philanthropic endeavours, click here.”

a3381.speaker: Archewell Foundation website
a3381.name: Archewell Foundation website
a3381.speech: States that the project tries to create “a safe haven and inclusive environment for women who have recently resettled in the US from Afghanistan” ; “The Duchess joined the Southern California Welcome Project for an evening of cooking and storytelling” ; “In collaboration with The Archewell Foundation’s partner, Mina’s List, a group of 15 women gathered to cook traditional Afghan food including Ashak and Mantu” ; “Following meal preparations, the women sat down to discuss their personal stories and the support they find from this intergenerational group of women.”

a3438.speaker: People to People Development Aid Association (ADPP) (data/statistics presented by the NGO)
a3438.name: People to People Development Aid Association (ADPP) (data/statistics presented by the NGO)
a3438.speech: According to data to which Lusa had access, more than 108,000 people have received treatment for tuberculosis since 2019 in Mozambique; of the total 108,242 notified and treated, 10,547 were children. "The project reached 6,403,980 people with educational messages about tuberculosis, and screened 6,421,685 individuals, including children under 5," reads the data presented by the organisation, detailing that the initiative was funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) with a budget of US$25 million (€22.8 million). The document adds that the project, which included the diagnosis and treatment of tuberculosis, was implemented in 50 districts in the provinces of Zambézia, Sofala and Tete, and in Nampula, and that it maintained and improved infrastructure in more than 20 health units.

a3438.speaker: Mozambican Ministry of Health
a3438.name: Mozambican Ministry of Health
a3438.speech: Indicated that Mozambique registered more than 116,000 cases of tuberculosis in 2023, compared to 119,000 in 2022, but the disease remains "an important public health challenge"; of the total 116,817 cases notified last year, 11% were diagnosed in children and a further 1,685 were resistant tuberculosis. "Up to 95% of patients were successfully treated in 2023," says the ministry, adding that drugs to treat the disease are available in all hospital units in the country.

a3438.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO) report
a3438.name: World Health Organisation (WHO) report
a3438.speech: According to a report released last year, in 2022 Mozambique recorded 5,300 deaths from tuberculosis and 119,000 cases of the disease; that year the WHO classified Mozambique and Angola as the Portuguese Language Countries with the highest number of tuberculosis cases.

a3438.speaker: Lusa (news agency)
a3438.name: Lusa (news agency)
a3438.speech: Previously reported that Mozambique registered more than 116,000 cases of tuberculosis in 2023, compared to 119,000 in 2022.

a3533.speaker: Stephen Azantilow, Director of Anti-Corruption, Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ)
a3533.name: Stephen Azantilow
a3533.title: Director of Anti-Corruption, Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ)
a3533.speech: Noted that the whole idea of Beneficial Ownership (BO) was to identify the people who were the real owners of companies; said often, people engaged in wrongdoing hide behind anonymous corporate structures, opaque financial systems and legal entities to engage in crimes such as fraud, money laundering and other illicit flow of money, and added that if the Registrar of Companies conducted those investigations, such people would be exposed ; “We need to begin to interrogate to know what type of assets they have and how they came by those assets. If we don't do these things, we will not get to know who the real BOs are because somebody can say, I'm a BO but he may be transacting the business on behalf of other persons. Monies may be coming to him, but for all you know, it is somebody else who is benefiting from those resources” ; said the law provides for verification of the information provided on beneficial ownership but the registrar of companies had not yet started it, and pointed out that verification was very important because it would help identify the real owners of a company and check crimes such as money laundering, terrorism and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction ; "Beneficial ownership transparency makes corruption easier to detect while making it a risky and unattractive venture."

a3533.speaker: Stephen Azantilow, Director of Anti-Corruption, CHRAJ
a3533.name: Stephen Azantilow
a3533.title: Director of Anti-Corruption, CHRAJ
a3533.speech: Warned those who were in the act of fronting for others with regard to the registration of owners of companies that under the Companies Act, they could be sanctioned.

a3533.speaker: Mary Awelana Addah, Executive Director of the Ghana Integrity Initiative (GII)
a3533.name: Mary Awelana Addah
a3533.title: Executive Director of the Ghana Integrity Initiative (GII)
a3533.speech: Explaining the rationale for the assessment, said it was, among others, aimed at assessing the legal regime, how enforcement had been done with regards to verification of beneficial ownership and assessing if there were effective interagency collaboration.

a3533.speaker: Mary Awelana Addah, Executive Director of GII (quoting the United Nations)
a3533.name: Mary Awelana Addah
a3533.title: Executive Director of GII (quoting the United Nations)
a3533.speech: Quoting the United Nations, Mrs Addah said Africa lost an estimated 88.6 billion annually to illicit financial flows, a figure that was nearly equivalent to what the continent received in official development assistance.

a3533.speaker: Michael Kwame Boadi (presenting the GII assessment findings)
a3533.name: Michael Kwame Boadi (presenting the GII assessment findings)
a3533.speech: Said the assessment found, among others, that BO information in the central register was available to relevant authorities and the public upon making a request, meaning that no relevant authority could access the information in the central register without the knowledge and approval of the registrar, which fell short of international standards and best practices ; said the assessment further found that the central register was not freely accessible, downloadable, searchable and reusable by the public, thereby going contrary to Act 992, which required access to BO information in the central register under open data principles.

a3533.speaker: Sandra Quarcoo, Director of Inspection and Compliance, Office of the Registrar of Companies
a3533.name: Sandra Quarcoo
a3533.title: Director of Inspection and Compliance, Office of the Registrar of Companies
a3533.speech: Said that to address the challenge of verification and sharing data in a form that was real-time and easily accessible by competent authorities, they would by the end of this year introduce a new software for all their registrations that would make it easy for their stakeholders and competent authorities to log in and get all the information they needed.

a3645.speaker: Cospas-Sarsat International Organisation (announcement)
a3645.name: Cospas-Sarsat International Organisation (announcement)
a3645.speech: Announced, during its virtual session on 13 June, the establishment of an international working group specialising in artificial intelligence applications in satellite search and rescue systems, following the meetings held in Abu Dhabi from 27 May to 5 June 2025.

a3645.speaker: National Guard Command, represented by the National Search and Rescue Centre (working document)
a3645.name: National Guard Command
a3645.title: represented by the National Search and Rescue Centre (working document)
a3645.speech: Presented the working document, on the basis of which the decision was taken, proposing the integration of artificial intelligence technologies into Mission Control Centre (MCC) operations, enhancing the effectiveness of rescue systems in space, and improving the speed and accuracy of responses to distress calls through smart data processing and integration into satellite networks.

a3645.speaker: Member states of the International Committee
a3645.name: Member states of the International Committee
a3645.speech: The UAE's initiative received extensive praise from the member states for its innovation and its progressive approach.

a3645.speaker: The International Committee
a3645.name: The International Committee
a3645.speech: Praised the UAE's role, its qualitative contribution and its proactive initiatives in harnessing modern technologies to serve international humanitarian rescue objectives.

a3703.speaker: Manqoba Khumalo, Minister for Commerce, Industry and Trade of Eswatini
a3703.name: Manqoba Khumalo
a3703.title: Minister for Commerce, Industry and Trade of Eswatini
a3703.speech: Speaking to Eswatini TV while attending the Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD), said Japan could serve as an alternative market for Eswatini's coal exports at a time when its primary market, South Africa, is in turmoil: “Japan has shown interest in taking Eswatini anthracite” ; “We are actively exploring Japan as another viable market for our coal, particularly in light of the challenges we are facing with South Africa's steel industry and energy-intensive sectors.”

a3703.speaker: Central Bank of Eswatini (CBE), Recent Economic Developments report
a3703.name: Central Bank of Eswatini (CBE)
a3703.title: Recent Economic Developments report
a3703.speech: Reported that coal production plunged by 31.5 per cent year-on-year in the first quarter of 2025, as part of a wider 28.9 per cent drop in the mining sector, with real GDP falling by 0.3 per cent on a seasonally adjusted basis, reversing the previous quarter's growth of 1.7 per cent.

a3703.speaker: Jabulile Shabangu, Chief Executive Officer of Maloma Colliery Limited
a3703.name: Jabulile Shabangu
a3703.title: Chief Executive Officer of Maloma Colliery Limited
a3703.speech: Said the power crisis in South Africa had slashed orders, leaving mines with unsold stockpiles: “Electricity costs have severely impacted smelters, forcing closures and reducing demand for our product” ; “This has undermined the viability of operations that once relied heavily on Eswatini's coal.”

a3703.speaker: Grindrod Logistics Eswatini
a3703.name: Grindrod Logistics Eswatini
a3703.speech: Revealed that export coal demand has dropped by nearly 50 per cent at its Sidvokodvo operations, idling about 200 Eswatini-owned trucks and putting transporters at risk of asset repossessions.

a3703.speaker: Mkhululi Dlamini, Grindrod Logistics Director
a3703.name: Mkhululi Dlamini
a3703.title: Grindrod Logistics Director
a3703.speech: “Falling coal demand has put us in a very difficult position. If the trend continues unchecked, retrenchments will deepen across the value chain. With Maloma already retrenching, fears are growing that the same could happen to our business.”

a3709.speaker: Edita Magileviciute, president of the Cape Verdean Ecotourism Association and mentor of the project
a3709.name: Edita Magileviciute
a3709.title: president of the Cape Verdean Ecotourism Association and mentor of the project
a3709.speech: Told Lusa that, besides the financial compensation for work it already knows how to do, it can be “one more educational tool” ; “One of the challenges is monitoring the process” so that the plastics correspond to the credits that can be accepted at the international level, and at Ekonatura that method “is almost ready” ; “But there were many interested parties”, including restaurants and other companies in the capital, which allowed the workshop to acquire a shredder and a press for producing sheets ; “A one-square-metre sheet contains 11.5 kilos of fully recycled and transformed plastic” ; “It is education in practice: what better example can there be for children? They sit on chairs made of 100% recycled plastic with bottle caps”, hoping that collaboration with institutions and companies will grow, because “there is a lot of potential”.

a3709.speaker: João Ferreira, manager of Ekonatura
a3709.name: João Ferreira
a3709.title: manager of Ekonatura
a3709.speech: “It is not easy to change deep-rooted habits”, describing the importance of residents as the drivers of change: “young people are the ones who react best, adults are not so easy to mould” ; says that now the idea is to “grow, extend the project to other communities”.

a3709.speaker: Rita Barros Silva, member of the Portuguese Association of Environmental Technology Companies (Apemeta)
a3709.name: Rita Barros Silva
a3709.title: member of the Portuguese Association of Environmental Technology Companies (Apemeta)
a3709.speech: Explained that all plastics collected from the environment can be subject to certification so as to enter the global market “in which companies integrate those credits into their sustainability strategies” ; told Lusa in September that “starting from the favourable contexts identified [beach clean-up campaigns, recycling and transformation projects], Cape Verdean actors can already begin to seek certification” in order then to obtain “financing for the continuity of their projects”.

a3709.speaker: Cipriana Lopes, Ekonatura collaborator
a3709.name: Cipriana Lopes
a3709.title: Ekonatura collaborator
a3709.speech: “All they have to do is support us, we are ready to continue”, she says, picking up the wheelbarrow to fill it again with plastic waste in São Francisco.

a3709.speaker: World Economic Forum (2016 forecast)
a3709.name: World Economic Forum (2016 forecast)
a3709.speech: Predicted, in 2016, that if trends continue, the oceans could have more plastic than fish by 2050.

a3709.speaker: World Bank (study published in June)
a3709.name: World Bank (study published in June)
a3709.speech: Explored the viability “of plastic credits as an emerging, results-based mechanism capable of linking public and private financing with specific activities to combat pollution”.

a3765.speaker: Abdoul Karim Diarra, Director of the National Directorate of Human Rights (DNDH) of Mali
a3765.name: Abdoul Karim Diarra
a3765.title: Director of the National Directorate of Human Rights (DNDH) of Mali
a3765.speech: Explained that the Human Rights Cafe initiative is in perfect coherence with the missions of the National Directorate of Human Rights (DNDH).

a3765.speaker: Oghale Oddo, Director of the USAID Mission in Mali
a3765.name: Oghale Oddo
a3765.title: Director of the USAID Mission in Mali
a3765.speech: Said the Human Rights Cafe is supported by the USAID Sariya Bato project, which will translate into a series of periodic meetings organised mainly in Bamako, with extensions to other regions depending on available resources, thereby allowing national reach and increased accessibility for remote populations.

a3765.speaker: Mamoudou Kassogue, Malian Minister of Justice, Human Rights and Keeper of the Seals
a3765.name: Mamoudou Kassogue
a3765.title: Malian Minister of Justice, Human Rights and Keeper of the Seals
a3765.speech: In his inaugural lecture, recalled that the history of humanity is made of highs and lows, divided between the continuous improvement of social organisation and production and scientific, technical and technological advances aiming at human happiness and fulfilment on the one hand, and the violence and atrocities that threaten human existence on the other - wars and their attendant miseries, famines, diseases, the exploitation and degradation of the human being, the seizure and destruction of natural resources, environmental degradation ; said that faced with these threats, the need was felt to maintain peace and justice in societies and to protect the human person, which is how human rights were constituted through Declarations, Covenants and Charters recognising fundamental rights that are universal, inalienable, indivisible and interdependent - civil and political rights, economic, social and cultural rights, and solidarity rights - for whose realisation individuals, social groups and States are responsible and of which States and the UN are the guarantors.

a3765.speaker: Mamoudou Kassogue, Malian Minister of Justice, Human Rights and Keeper of the Seals
a3765.name: Mamoudou Kassogue
a3765.title: Malian Minister of Justice, Human Rights and Keeper of the Seals
a3765.speech: Said that unfortunately, in many countries, resources and wealth are not equitably distributed and are the object of embezzlement through theft, breach of trust, fraud, forgery, corruption, extortion, favouritism, misuse of corporate assets, money laundering and illegal taking of interest ; explained that it is common knowledge that corruption destroys everything it touches, that the embezzlement of public funds has harmful consequences for the individual, society and the State, so that the State sees its credibility and legitimacy affected, society sees its bearings and values flouted, and individuals and groups see the realisation of their rights jeopardised - listing the impact of corruption on peace and security, on the quality of human resources (recruitment), on development projects (roads, agriculture), on access to water, energy and food, in the mining sector, on health, on education, on the environment, on land, on economic growth, on inequalities, on citizens' trust, on the effectiveness of institutions and on the electoral process.

a3853.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3853.name: Donald Trump
a3853.title: US President
a3853.speech: has just announced the imminent exit of his country from UNESCO without further ado.

a3853.speaker: Article 55 of the 2023 Constitution of Mali (document)
a3853.name: Article 55 of the 2023 Constitution of Mali (document)
a3853.speech: provides that the President of the Transition should renew his oath of office before Mali and Malians through the Supreme Court.

a3853.speaker: Certain sources (anonymous)
a3853.name: Certain sources (anonymous)
a3853.speech: indicate that the occupant of Koulouba could comply next week with the formality of recalling his missions and responsibilities as head of state.

a4134.speaker: Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India (announcement during his 2018 visit to Uganda)
a4134.name: Narendra Modi
a4134.title: Prime Minister of India (announcement during his 2018 visit to Uganda)
a4134.speech: Announced that “Africa will be at the top of our priorities and we will continue to intensify and deepen our engagement with Africa”.

a4134.speaker: Government of India (decision / joint initiative of the Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Defence)
a4134.name: Government of India (decision / joint initiative of the Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Defence)
a4134.speech: Decided to provide 270 tonnes of humanitarian aid to friendly countries such as the Republic of Sudan, the Republic of South Sudan, the Republic of Djibouti and the State of Eritrea, which have been affected by natural disasters, as part of the SAGAR II framework.

a4151.speaker: Christopher J. Lamora, U.S. Ambassador to Cameroon
a4151.name: Christopher J. Lamora
a4151.title: U.S. Ambassador to Cameroon
a4151.speech: In his meeting with the Governor of the Southwest Region, emphasized the importance of peace and stability as cornerstones of sustainable development, acknowledging the government’s efforts to improve the lives of its citizens in major towns in the region.

a4151.speaker: Christopher J. Lamora, U.S. Ambassador to Cameroon
a4151.name: Christopher J. Lamora
a4151.title: U.S. Ambassador to Cameroon
a4151.speech: While speaking on a panel at the Cameroon International Film Festival (CAMIFF), emphasized the film industry’s vital contribution to local economies; applauded CAMIFF Founder Gilbert Agbor Ebot for fostering collaborations between Cameroonian and American filmmakers.

a4151.speaker: Christopher J. Lamora, U.S. Ambassador to Cameroon
a4151.name: Christopher J. Lamora
a4151.title: U.S. Ambassador to Cameroon
a4151.speech: Praised the Limbe Wildlife Center’s conservation efforts — not only for protecting Cameroon’s rich biodiversity but also for supporting public health education, enhancing community livelihoods and instilling respect for the environment in Cameroon’s next generation.

a4151.speaker: Christopher J. Lamora, U.S. Ambassador to Cameroon
a4151.name: Christopher J. Lamora
a4151.title: U.S. Ambassador to Cameroon
a4151.speech: Reaffirmed the U.S. Embassy’s enduring commitment to peace, prosperity, and partnership with Cameroon ; acknowledging the collective effort behind the health achievements at Mutengene Baptist Hospital, reaffirmed the United States’ long-term commitment to strengthening health security in Cameroon.

a4151.speaker: Bernard Ngone, Director of the Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration (DDR) Centre in Tiko
a4151.name: Bernard Ngone
a4151.title: Director of the Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration (DDR) Centre in Tiko
a4151.speech: Described the centre’s efforts to reintegrating ex-combatants through vocational training, moral education, and strong collaboration with local communities.

a4151.speaker: Colonel Henri Belinga, Cameroon's Rapid Intervention Battalion (BIR)
a4151.name: Colonel Henri Belinga
a4151.title: Cameroon's Rapid Intervention Battalion (BIR)
a4151.speech: In discussions with the Ambassador, described the BIR’s strides in professionalizing its forces and enhancing training on the law of armed conflict and respect for internationally recognized human rights.

a4151.speaker: Thomas Ndive Mulongo, Deputy Director of the Transitional Administration, Port Authority of Limbe
a4151.name: Thomas Ndive Mulongo
a4151.title: Deputy Director of the Transitional Administration, Port Authority of Limbe
a4151.speech: Discussed infrastructure projects with the Ambassador, including the proposed significant expansion of the Port of Limbe, the potential for public-private partnerships and ways to leverage U.S. expertise in maritime risk management and port operations.

a4151.speaker: Paramount Chiefs of Buea and Limbe
a4151.name: Paramount Chiefs of Buea and Limbe
a4151.speech: Conferred honors upon the Ambassador and shared updates on their community-driven initiatives, including waste management, workforce development, and other local priorities.

a4151.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Cameroon (report distributed by the APO Group)
a4151.name: U.S. Embassy in Cameroon (report distributed by the APO Group)
a4151.speech: Noted that the visit underscored that, as stability takes hold, the Southwest Region is unlocking new opportunities for dynamic U.S.–Cameroon collaboration.

a4158.speaker: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4158.name: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4158.speech: Assured that, from that moment on, Cabo Verdeans would be able to plan trips, production and business with confidence.

a4158.speaker: Arbitral tribunal (ruling)
a4158.name: Arbitral tribunal (ruling)
a4158.speech: Ordered the State of Cabo Verde to pay compensation which, to date, already amounts to at least 19 million euros.

a4158.speaker: Adam Smith
a4158.name: Adam Smith
a4158.speech: Recalled that it is not from the benevolence of the baker or the butcher that we expect our dinner, but rather from their regard to their own interest.

a4158.speaker: Joseph Schumpeter
a4158.name: Joseph Schumpeter
a4158.speech: Reinforced the same logic by explaining that capitalism renews itself through the incessant search for new opportunities for profit.

a4158.speaker: Milton Friedman
a4158.name: Milton Friedman
a4158.speech: Stated that the social responsibility of business is to increase its profits.

a4158.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a4158.name: Olavo Correia
a4158.title: Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a4158.speech: Said that Cabo Verde would have “money that never runs out.”

a4162.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) communiqué
a4162.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) communiqué
a4162.speech: Reported that in Niger the economic outlook is favourable in the short term, with growth projected at 8.8% for 2024, growth that will be “supported by oil exports, the lifting of sanctions and a good agricultural season” ; added that “the authorities’ continued efforts to simplify the tax system and to adopt a strategy for managing oil revenues are essential reforms to create fiscal space to meet development spending needs” ; warned that “this positive outlook is subject to downside risks” ; “Growth is projected at 8.8% in 2024, driven mainly by oil exports, by a favourable agricultural campaign and by the lifting of sanctions. Economic activity should remain dynamic next year, with growth reaching 7.9%, while inflation should fall back to 3.7%” ; cautioned that “the risks surrounding this outlook are tilted to the downside. A deterioration of security conditions could weigh further on economic activity, while fiscal space could shrink if regional financing conditions continue to tighten” ; “Among the other external risks are the volatility of commodity prices and the economic fallout of an escalation of regional conflicts (such as tensions in the Middle East).”

a4162.speaker: Antonio David, head of the IMF delegation
a4162.name: Antonio David
a4162.title: head of the IMF delegation
a4162.speech: Stated at the end of the mission that “the Nigerien authorities and the IMF team have reached a staff-level agreement on the sixth review of the economic programme supported by the Extended Credit Facility, on the second review of the arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility, and have conducted the 2024 Article IV consultations” ; “The staff-level agreement will be submitted for the approval of IMF Management and the Executive Board... Completion of the ECF review would allow a disbursement of SDR 13.16 million (about 17.4 million dollars, or 10% of Niger’s quota) to cover the country’s external financing needs” ; “In addition, completion of the second review of the arrangement under the RSF would allow an additional disbursement of SDR 25.66 million (about 34 million dollars, or 19.5% of Niger’s quota)” ; “Despite a delicate context owing to certain factors such as the human and material consequences of the recent floods, liquidity tensions in the banking sector and tight financing conditions, a strong recovery of economic activity is expected this year.”

a4281.speaker: Miles Pattenden, historian of the Catholic church at Oxford University
a4281.name: Miles Pattenden
a4281.title: historian of the Catholic church at Oxford University
a4281.speech: "In fact, conversations have probably been going on for some time, certainly since the start of this year, because the trajectory of Pope Francis's health has been clear," said Miles Pattenden.

a4281.speaker: Gerhard Müller, German cardinal
a4281.name: Gerhard Müller
a4281.title: German cardinal
a4281.speech: Warned last week that the church could split if an orthodox pope is not elected.

a4281.speaker: Critics of Pope Francis
a4281.name: Critics of Pope Francis
a4281.speech: Accused Francis of packing the college of cardinals with his supporters in making more than 100 appointments during his papacy.

a4281.speaker: Miles Pattenden, historian of the Catholic church at Oxford University
a4281.name: Miles Pattenden
a4281.title: historian of the Catholic church at Oxford University
a4281.speech: "Historically, no pope has been able to control the election of his successor. There were clear conservatives and progressives among the cardinals, but it's a spectrum. There are some who hold conservative views on certain issues but liberal views on other issues - for example, sexuality and climate change: Francis was more inclined to promote his ideological confreres, but he didn't exclusively appoint those who appeared to agree with him. He had other priorities - to make the college of cardinals as inclusive as possible, which meant choosing men from very small Catholic communities like Iran and Algeria and Mongolia and balancing it away from its rich European and North American heartlands."

a4281.speaker: Miles Pattenden, historian of the Catholic church at Oxford University
a4281.name: Miles Pattenden
a4281.title: historian of the Catholic church at Oxford University
a4281.speech: Said the cardinals will be "under quite a lot of pressure to choose quite quickly". "The world's eyes are on them, and the Catholic faithful might find it a bit disconcerting if they're still in the conclave in June or in July."

a4281.speaker: Leighton Vaughan Williams, professor of economics and finance at Nottingham Business School
a4281.name: Leighton Vaughan Williams
a4281.title: professor of economics and finance at Nottingham Business School
a4281.speech: Told AFP: "What was once a pursuit confined largely to Renaissance Roman bankers and courtiers has evolved into a multimillion-dollar global market accessible at the click of a button or a tap on a crypto wallet." ; He said the speed with which betting activity had taken off this year "underscores an enduring cultural fascination with the papacy, amplified by media coverage and popular culture".

a4281.speaker: Luis Antonio Tagle, Filipino cardinal, former archbishop of Manila
a4281.name: Luis Antonio Tagle
a4281.title: Filipino cardinal, former archbishop of Manila
a4281.speech: Has suggested that the Catholic church's stance on gay and divorced couples is too harsh, but has opposed abortion rights in the Philippines.

a4281.speaker: Peter Turkson, Ghanaian cardinal
a4281.name: Peter Turkson
a4281.title: Ghanaian cardinal
a4281.speech: Has been vocal on issues such as the climate crisis, poverty and economic justice while affirming the church's traditional positions on the priesthood, marriage between a man and a woman, and homosexuality; has argued that laws in many African countries are too harsh, and has spoken out on corruption and human rights.

a4281.speaker: Péter Erdő, Hungarian cardinal
a4281.name: Péter Erdő
a4281.title: Hungarian cardinal
a4281.speech: Has been a strong advocate for traditional Catholic teachings and doctrine; in 2015 he appeared to align himself with Hungary's nationalist prime minister, Viktor Orbán, when he opposed Francis's call for churches to take in migrants.

a4281.speaker: George Pell, late cardinal
a4281.name: George Pell
a4281.title: late cardinal
a4281.speech: Believed Erdő would restore the rule of law in the post-Francis Vatican.

a4281.speaker: Mario Grech, Maltese cardinal
a4281.name: Mario Grech
a4281.title: Maltese cardinal
a4281.speech: Has criticised European political leaders who sought to limit the activities of NGO ships and has expressed support for female deacons.

a4281.speaker: Pierbattista Pizzaballa, Latin patriarch of Jerusalem
a4281.name: Pierbattista Pizzaballa
a4281.title: Latin patriarch of Jerusalem
a4281.speech: After Hamas's attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, offered himself as a hostage in exchange for children who were being held by Hamas in Gaza.

a4281.speaker: Robert Sarah, Guinean cardinal
a4281.name: Robert Sarah
a4281.title: Guinean cardinal
a4281.speech: In 2020 co-authored a book with the then retired Pope Benedict defending clerical celibacy that was seen as a challenge to Francis's authority; has denounced "gender ideology" as a threat to society, and has spoken out against Islamic fundamentalism.

a4281.speaker: Vatican observer (anonymous)
a4281.name: Vatican observer (anonymous)
a4281.speech: According to the observer, Sarah at one time sought to present himself as a "parallel authority" to Francis.

a4296.speaker: Donald Trump’s campaign manifesto
a4296.name: Donald Trump’s campaign manifesto
a4296.speech: Has again hinted at fostering trade agreements that prioritise reciprocity.

a4296.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a4296.name: Donald Trump
a4296.title: US President-elect
a4296.speech: Has been vocal about his intention to combat terrorism, an agenda that could continue in Africa.

a4384.speaker: Apple
a4384.name: Apple
a4384.speech: Says it is shifting production of most iPhones and other devices to be sold in the US away from China, which has been the focus of President Donald Trump’s tariffs ; estimated that US import taxes could add about $900m (£677.5m) to its costs in the current quarter, despite Trump’s decision to spare key electronics from the new tariffs ; said revenues for the first three months of the year rose 5% from the same period last year, to $95.4bn.

a4384.speaker: Tim Cook, Apple chief executive
a4384.name: Tim Cook
a4384.title: Apple chief executive
a4384.speech: Says the majority of the iPhones bound for the US market in the coming months will be made in India, while Vietnam will be a major production hub for items like iPads and Apple Watches ; opened the discussion with a reminder of the company’s plans to invest $500bn across several US states over the next four years ; “We do expect the majority of iPhones sold in US will have India as their country of origin” ; said Vietnam will be the chief manufacturing hub “for almost all iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and AirPods product sold in the US” ; added that China will remain the country of origin for the vast majority of total products sold outside the US.

a4384.speaker: The Trump administration
a4384.name: The Trump administration
a4384.speech: Has repeatedly said it wants Apple to move production to America.

a4384.speaker: Shanti Kelemen, chief investment officer at M&G Wealth
a4384.name: Shanti Kelemen
a4384.title: chief investment officer at M&G Wealth
a4384.speech: Told the BBC’s Today programme: “There will still be tariffs that impact the supply chains [for Apple] and a cost to move them and build new factories. Apple have said they want to invest $500bn over the next few years.”

a4384.speaker: Amazon
a4384.name: Amazon
a4384.speech: Said sales were holding up, rising 8% year-on-year in its North America e-commerce business in the most recent quarter, and forecast similar growth in the months ahead ; said it was working to make sure it had a diversity of sellers ; said overall sales jumped 9% to $155.7bn in the first three months of 2025, while profits surged more than 60% year-on-year to roughly $17bn.

a4384.speaker: Andy Jassy, Amazon boss
a4384.name: Andy Jassy
a4384.title: Amazon boss
a4384.speech: “Obviously no one of us knows exactly where tariffs will settle or when,” while noting that the firm has emerged from periods of disruption – like the pandemic – stronger than before ; “We’re often able to weather challenging conditions better than others. I’m optimistic this could happen again.” ; said he felt the firm was well-positioned for the months ahead, pointing to the firm’s scale and its role supplying everyday essentials.

a4384.speaker: Patrick Moorhead, chief executive of Moor Insights & Strategy
a4384.name: Patrick Moorhead
a4384.title: chief executive of Moor Insights & Strategy
a4384.speech: Said the shift of the iPhone supply chain to India was “impressive” ; “This is a marked change from what [Cook] said a few years back when he said that only China can build iPhones” ; “There is lots of progress that Apple must show here but it’s a pretty good start.”

a4384.speaker: Amazon executives
a4384.name: Amazon executives
a4384.speech: Said the business may have benefited from some customers starting to stockpile.

a4526.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a4526.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a4526.title: President of Liberia
a4526.speech: Says he will no longer participate in dedication of hand pumps, noting that such action no longer aligns with the nation’s aspirations after 178 years of Independence: “I said, for me, we will never dedicate hand pumps again. Because for 178 years, we have passed that age.”

a4526.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a4526.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a4526.title: President of Liberia
a4526.speech: Emphasizes the importance of meaningful development, stating that it’s time to do things properly for the benefit of the people, and stresses that he does not want his name on any public project, declaring that he was elected to serve, not to seek praises: “Our job is to improve the lives of the people, to give them decent facilities. I don’t want my name on anything. This is not the first time; we’ve done the same in parts of Lofa County and other areas.”

a4526.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a4526.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a4526.title: President of Liberia
a4526.speech: Pledges that his administration would focus on improving infrastructure, especially roads and access to clean water, and vows to prioritize “farm-to-market” roads to help farmers transport their goods: “We’re going to make good roads, ensure access to safe drinking water, and use the country’s money to build up our people” ; “We cannot keep going to other countries for a better life. God has given us everything we need. It’s time to build this country for the future.” ; encourages all Liberians to actively contribute to national development, urging them to appreciate good initiatives and support the ongoing work.

a4526.speaker: Cytarus G. Dahn, Coordinator of the Presidential Special Project
a4526.name: Cytarus G. Dahn
a4526.title: Coordinator of the Presidential Special Project
a4526.speech: Provides an overview of the market renovation, noting that marketers had written to President Boakai requesting assistance and that in response her team engaged several partners, including NOCAL, the National Port Authority (NPA), and NASSCORP, among others, that contributed a total of US$98,000 to the project; says other markets across Liberia are also slated to benefit under the Presidential Special Project, which is being implemented by Cytarus Initiative.

a4526.speaker: Elizabeth Finda Sambollah, National President of the Liberia Marketing Association (LMA)
a4526.name: Elizabeth Finda Sambollah
a4526.title: National President of the Liberia Marketing Association (LMA)
a4526.speech: Expresses gratitude, calling the initiative a clear demonstration of the President’s commitment to market women across the country, and appeals for additional support, including a new site for the ELWA Market and more projects in Paynesville and beyond.

a4594.speaker: World Bank (projection)
a4594.name: World Bank (projection)
a4594.speech: Projects that success could unlock Africa's contribution to the global economy to the tune of $6.5 trillion in economic potential by 2030, while failure to act threatens an estimated $17 trillion in lifetime learning losses across low and middle-income countries globally.

a4594.speaker: African Ministers of Education (22 Ministers and 12 Heads of Ministerial Delegations from 34 countries, FLEX 2024 declaration)
a4594.name: African Ministers of Education (22 Ministers and 12 Heads of Ministerial Delegations from 34 countries
a4594.title: FLEX 2024 declaration)
a4594.speech: Endorsed the African Union's call to declare a 'Decade of Education' and issued a five-point declaration committing to: set and achieve a continental target of zero learning poverty by 2035; fully endorse and implement the African Union's Decade of Education initiative; establish robust inter-country collaboration frameworks; scale evidence-based interventions through efficient resource allocation; and implement comprehensive data and accountability mechanisms.

a4594.speaker: Jeanette Kagame, First Lady of the Republic of Rwanda
a4594.name: Jeanette Kagame
a4594.title: First Lady of the Republic of Rwanda
a4594.speech: Said in her keynote address: "Reading and comprehension of simple texts is still an issue for 9 out of 10 children aged 10 and below, in the majority of African countries. What a loud alarm bell this statistic rings! Should we fail to strengthen Foundational Learning and critical thinking, increase primary education completion rates, and allocate more resources to education, specifically to the more vulnerable learners, what is to be the long-term cost to the youth of this continent, their skills development, employability, and social welfare?"

a4594.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia and Africa Champion of Foundational Learning
a4594.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a4594.title: President of Zambia and Africa Champion of Foundational Learning
a4594.speech: Said in his address: "We need to start thinking more strategically about innovative models of funding education and to use our resources more effectively. We need to implement evidence-based approaches and scale what works to improve foundational learning on the continent and we need robust accountability mechanisms at national, regional, and continental levels for both partners and governments."

a4607.speaker: Dr Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Health Minister
a4607.name: Dr Kalumbi Shangula
a4607.title: Namibian Health Minister
a4607.speech: “We gathered here today for a very special occasion to witness the commissioning of a purpose-built boat, designed to facilitate the transportation of health workers and patients on the water course.” ; said that the donation marks a significant milestone in Namibia's ongoing mission to provide integrated, affordable and quality healthcare services ; “The geography of the Zambezi Region presents unique challenges, particularly during the rainy season when flooding disrupts access to essential health services.” ; added the boat is a targeted solution to ensure that all citizens, irrespective of location, have access to necessary healthcare services ; “Namibia's UHC Service Coverage Index currently stands at 63%—one of the highest in the SADC region.”

a4607.speaker: Dr Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Health Minister
a4607.name: Dr Kalumbi Shangula
a4607.title: Namibian Health Minister
a4607.speech: Recognising the growing impact of climate change on healthcare service delivery, underscored the need for innovative solutions: “Recurrent floods not only disrupt everyday life but also hinder critical healthcare services. This boat is not just a mode of transport – it is a lifeline. It can make a huge difference in maternal and child health services, as well as in managing disease outbreaks.”

a4607.speaker: Bernhard Sisamu, Kabbe North constituency councillor
a4607.name: Bernhard Sisamu
a4607.title: Kabbe North constituency councillor
a4607.speech: Echoed Shangula's sentiments, urging local communities to take responsibility for maintaining the donated boat: “This boat is an invaluable resource, and it is imperative that we all take ownership of it. Let us work together to safeguard and maintain it so that it can serve us for many years to come.”

a4609.speaker: US State Department
a4609.name: US State Department
a4609.speech: Announced on Wednesday that it will reduce the budgetary allocation of USAID's foreign development programmes and multi-year contracts by 92 per cent; said the contract and foreign assistance programmes to be eliminated total $54 billion, and that the slash is part of a review to significantly reduce US foreign assistance to countries. “At the conclusion of a process led by USAID leadership, including tranches personally reviewed by Secretary Marco Rubio, nearly 5,800 awards with $54 billion in value remaining were identified for elimination as part of the America First agenda – a 92 per cent reduction.” ; also stated that another 9,100 grants involving foreign assistance, estimated to cost more than $15.9 billion, will be reviewed, after which another 4,100 grants worth almost $4.4 billion may be eliminated.

a4609.speaker: US State Department
a4609.name: US State Department
a4609.speech: Stated that the review will not affect programmes focused on providing food assistance, life-saving medical treatments for diseases like HIV and malaria, and support for countries such as Haiti, Cuba, Venezuela and Lebanon.

a4609.speaker: Al Jazeera
a4609.name: Al Jazeera
a4609.speech: Cited as the source of the State Department statement.

a4609.speaker: Nigerian federal government
a4609.name: Nigerian federal government
a4609.speech: Says it is committed to bridging the funding gap created by the new US government; on 3 February, the Federal Executive Council (FEC) approved $1.07 billion to finance healthcare sector reforms under the Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity (HOPE) programme.

a4609.speaker: Wale Edun, Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a4609.name: Wale Edun
a4609.title: Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a4609.speech: Disclosed that FEC also approved N4.8 billion for HIV treatment (as reported by PREMIUM TIMES).

a4609.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a4609.name: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a4609.speech: Announced that it plans to strengthen its domestic HIV response and also produce HIV-related medical tools, including test kits and antiretroviral drugs.

a4609.speaker: Nigerian Senate
a4609.name: Nigerian Senate
a4609.speech: Recently allocated an additional N300 billion to the health sector in the 2025 budget, equivalent to $200 million, targeting health programmes such as Tuberculosis, HIV, Malaria and Polio.

a4644.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a4644.name: World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a4644.speech: Said Tuesday that one of Myanmar's most conflict-ravaged regions has witnessed a "dramatic rise in hunger" after US aid cuts pushed by President Donald Trump during a punishing civil war; said that in central Rakhine 57 percent of families are now unable to meet their basic food needs, a rise of 24 percent since December. "A deadly combination of conflict, blockades, and funding cuts is driving a dramatic rise in hunger and malnutrition." ; Said it is believed "the situation in northern Rakhine is much worse due to active conflict and access issues".

a4644.speaker: Michael Dunford, WFP Myanmar director
a4644.name: Michael Dunford
a4644.title: WFP Myanmar director
a4644.speech: "People are trapped in a vicious cycle; cut off by conflict, stripped of livelihoods, and left with no humanitarian safety net. Without urgent action, this crisis will spiral into a full-blown disaster."

a4699.speaker: Neimatu Adjabui, PQM+ programme manager for West Africa
a4699.name: Neimatu Adjabui
a4699.title: PQM+ programme manager for West Africa
a4699.speech: Explained that the objective of the workshop is to strengthen the capacities of the national pharmaceutical regulatory authority and the LNSP in order to ensure the good quality of medicines on the market ; “During this meeting, we are going to discuss the problems of quality assurance of medicines in order to improve our intervention for better results. We have noticed that there are at all times substandard and falsified medicines on the market, and that is why this workshop was initiated.” ; revealed that it will be an opportunity for all the participants to make known their role in the field of quality assurance of medicines, as well as to set out the problems they face, in order to propose solutions that will be evaluated.

a4699.speaker: Dr Anicet Soubeiga, pharmacist specialising in quality management systems, resource person
a4699.name: Dr Anicet Soubeiga
a4699.title: pharmacist specialising in quality management systems, resource person
a4699.speech: “This workshop aims to bring coherence to the quality-assurance activities carried out by the various services empowered to do so in the field of medicines, in order to put in place a health quality-assurance strategy that will continuously guarantee effective medicines for the population.” ; according to him, despite the work done by the authorised services, products of doubtful quality manage to be sold on the markets; he explained that it is difficult to control everything, because it is a whole chain from production through to the sale of the products ; “The expected results of this workshop are to identify our strengths together in order to chart perspectives and to lay the foundations for a strategy that will make it possible to ensure the quality of the products sold on the market.” ; invited the various participants to stand shoulder to shoulder in order to achieve the objectives, so as to reassure the population about the quality of these products.

a4754.speaker: Adrienne Watson, spokesperson for the (US) National Security Council (statement)
a4754.name: Adrienne Watson
a4754.title: spokesperson for the (US) National Security Council (statement)
a4754.speech: “These measures, which include the commitment to open the port of Ashdod, the opening of the Erez crossing point and the significant increase in aid deliveries from Jordan directly into Gaza, must now be implemented quickly and completely.”

a4754.speaker: Office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (statement)
a4754.name: Office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (statement)
a4754.speech: Had earlier announced that Israel will temporarily allow the delivery of humanitarian aid into the famine-stricken Gaza Strip through the port of Ashdod and the Erez crossing point ; said the war cabinet authorised the Government to “take immediate measures to increase humanitarian aid” with the aim of “avoiding a humanitarian crisis” and “ensuring the continuation of the fighting.”

a4754.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a4754.name: Joe Biden
a4754.title: US President
a4754.speech: Told the Israeli prime minister on Thursday that the future of North American support for Israel’s war in Gaza depended on the adoption of new measures to protect civilians and humanitarian workers.

a4754.speaker: France-Presse count based on official Israeli data
a4754.name: France-Presse count based on official Israeli data
a4754.speech: 1,170 people were killed on the Israeli side in the 7 October Hamas attack, most of them civilians killed on the same day.

a4754.speaker: Gaza Health Ministry, controlled by the Islamist movement Hamas
a4754.name: Gaza Health Ministry
a4754.title: controlled by the Islamist movement Hamas
a4754.speech: Israel’s retaliatory military operation in Gaza has already caused more than 33,000 deaths, most of them civilians.

a4782.speaker: Jesus (Matthew 19:17)
a4782.name: Jesus (Matthew 19:17)
a4782.speech: Says, "No one is good but One, that is, God."

a4782.speaker: David (Psalm 16:2)
a4782.name: David (Psalm 16:2)
a4782.speech: Says, "Lord, You are my Lord, my goodness is nothing apart from You."

a4782.speaker: Jesus (Matthew 13:44-46)
a4782.name: Jesus (Matthew 13:44-46)
a4782.speech: "Again, the kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid; and for joy over it he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field. Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking beautiful pearls, who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had and bought it."

a4782.speaker: David (Psalms 57:2)
a4782.name: David (Psalms 57:2)
a4782.speech: "I will cry out to God Most High, to God who performs all things for me."

a4782.speaker: Jesus (John 15:5)
a4782.name: Jesus (John 15:5)
a4782.speech: Says, "I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing."

a4782.speaker: Isaiah (Isaiah 65:24)
a4782.name: Isaiah (Isaiah 65:24)
a4782.speech: "It shall come to pass that before they call, I will answer; and while they are still speaking, I will hear."

a4782.speaker: Jesus (Matthew 22:37)
a4782.name: Jesus (Matthew 22:37)
a4782.speech: Says, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind."

a4841.speaker: Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) and Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP), joint position
a4841.name: Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) and Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP)
a4841.title: joint position
a4841.speech: Both parties reaffirmed their commitment to working together more effectively to address challenges and capitalize on opportunities for revenue growth through the full implementation of the country's revenue laws ; concluded the meeting reaffirming their shared commitment to revenue mobilization as a fundamental pillar of Liberia's economic stability and development.

a4841.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a4841.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a4841.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a4841.speech: "We have come to receive an update on revenue performance and gain deeper insights into the challenges you face. Our goal is to work collaboratively to enhance revenue generation and drive national development," Minister Ngafuan stated during the engagement.

a4841.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a4841.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a4841.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a4841.speech: Commended the LRA for exceeding its 2024 revenue target, having surpassed the projected US$690 million in domestic revenue by collecting over US$693 million, and expressed optimism for sustained growth and stronger fiscal management in the years ahead.

a4841.speaker: James Dorbor Jallah, Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority
a4841.name: James Dorbor Jallah
a4841.title: Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority
a4841.speech: Acknowledged the Ministry's continued support, which he credited as a key factor in the LRA's success ; outlined a couple of challenges and emphasized the need for increased budgetary allocation to address them and to enable the Authority to meet its ambitious domestic revenue target of US$804.6 million for 2025.

a4885.speaker: Participants of Capital Newspaper's COVID-19 webinar
a4885.name: Participants of Capital Newspaper's COVID-19 webinar
a4885.speech: said that the session was helpful in terms of understanding and handling stress in this difficult time.

a4885.speaker: Yene H. K. Assegid, Transformative Leadership Coach and Trainer
a4885.name: Yene H. K. Assegid
a4885.title: Transformative Leadership Coach and Trainer
