a4885.speech: highlighted that the worldwide outbreak of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) is a source of unexpected stress and adversity for many people ; “Resilience can help us get through and overcome hardship. But resilience is not something we are born with-it’s built over time as the experiences we have interact with our unique, individual genetic makeup. That’s why we all respond to stress and adversity-like that from the COVID-19 pandemic-differently.” ; “The main point is to try to stay positive. Unload the negative side,” she stressed to the participants.

a4885.speaker: Teguest Yilma, Managing Director of Capital Newspaper
a4885.name: Teguest Yilma
a4885.title: Managing Director of Capital Newspaper
a4885.speech: “The sessions are organized with our readers at heart, whom we value very much.” ; “Capital’s journalistic mission and vision is always disseminating valuable information but also enriching society with the exchange of ideas. COVID-19 has dealt us with an unprecedented situation where we are all obliged to step up our capacity to cope. We will get through this together.”

a4999.speaker: Hon. Dr. Gada James, lawmaker representing Yei River County in the Transitional National Legislative Assembly (SPLM)
a4999.name: Hon. Dr. Gada James
a4999.title: lawmaker representing Yei River County in the Transitional National Legislative Assembly (SPLM)
a4999.speech: Urged an urgent appeal for humanitarian assistance, raising the alarm during a sitting of the Assembly and reporting that rebel attacks in parts of Yei River County, specifically in Pakula Boma and Mugo Payam, have forced more than 400 households to flee their homes; she said displaced families from areas such as Marjub, under Korobe Mountain, have taken refuge in Pakula Centre, and detailed how armed groups attacked villages in Pakula and Longamere, burning homes and overpowering local forces: "They chased the government soldiers out of the area and burned homes. Now our people are scattered, terrified, and in desperate need of help." ; "Honorable Speaker, there are many displaced people in my constituency. These families—women, children, and the elderly, are now sleeping in the forests of Mugo and Pakula, with nothing." ; "They have no food, no shelter, and no medical help. We must act—urgently." ; "Let us not wait. These people are suffering now. They need urgent humanitarian support before anything else." ; She urged the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and the Assembly's Committee for Humanitarian Affairs to act swiftly and deliver emergency support to the affected communities.

a4999.speaker: Speaker of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly
a4999.name: Speaker of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly
a4999.speech: In response, acknowledged the concern and directed the matter to be handled through the appropriate committee and coordinated with the Ministry.

a5024.speaker: Akinwumi A. Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5024.name: Akinwumi A. Adesina
a5024.title: President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5024.speech: Said in his lecture that in the wake of a rapidly changing global landscape, time has come for Africa to wean itself from aid dependency and chart its future through self-reliance, strategic partnerships and exploiting its vast natural resources ; “The era of aid or free money is gone. African countries must now learn to develop via investment discipline. Countries can no longer rely on aid for growth or count it as part of government revenue, as has been the case for decades. Benevolence is not an asset class.”

a5024.speaker: The Nation (January 29 2025 edition)
a5024.name: The Nation (January 29 2025 edition)
a5024.speech: Reported that $284.7 million (about K493.7 billion) financing through USAid to Malawi is at stake.

a5024.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs of Malawi
a5024.name: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs of Malawi
a5024.speech: Said of the amount, US contribution to the 2024/25 National Budget stood at K9.2 billion of the expected K1.17 trillion projected grants.

a5024.speaker: World Bank Group
a5024.name: World Bank Group
a5024.speech: Describes trade as a golden key towards ending global poverty because countries that are open to international trade tend to grow faster, become innovative, improve productivity and provide higher income as well as more opportunities.

a5062.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a5062.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a5062.speech: “Despite the 1 March 2026 deadline for 37 NGOs to leave Palestine, MSF is committed to remaining to provide assistance. Under international humanitarian law, the Israeli authorities, as the occupying power, are obliged to ensure the provision of humanitarian assistance. Governments worldwide must ensure…”

a5062.speaker: A3 group of African members of the UN Security Council (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Liberia and Somalia)
a5062.name: A3 group of African members of the UN Security Council (Democratic Republic of the Congo
a5062.title: Liberia and Somalia)
a5062.speech: Condemned attacks on humanitarian assets in Sudan, including a recent strike on a World Food Programme convoy attributed to elements…

a5062.speaker: Herbert Mensah, President of Rugby Africa and member of World Rugby's Executive Board
a5062.name: Herbert Mensah
a5062.title: President of Rugby Africa and member of World Rugby's Executive Board
a5062.speech: Praised Kenya for delivering a world-class HSBC SVNS 2 tournament in Nairobi, describing the event as a statement…

a5062.speaker: Sergey Lavrov, Russian Foreign Minister
a5062.name: Sergey Lavrov
a5062.title: Russian Foreign Minister
a5062.speech: Has reiterated the official statement on expanding ‘visa-free’ travel between Russia and Africa, signaling the Kremlin's earlier position on facilitating people-to-people movement and raising cultural interaction.

a5062.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a5062.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a5062.speech: Strongly condemns the recent attacks on its river convoy in Upper Nile State over the weekend; WFP has suspended all activities in Baliet County until the safety and security of its staff, partners and contractors is assured.

a5062.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a5062.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a5062.speech: Is today calling on all parties to the conflict to urgently halt military operations, de-escalate the situation, and allow safe humanitarian access to deliver life-saving food assistance to hundreds of thousands of people in South Sudan.

a5149.speaker: Prosecutors (US federal prosecutors)
a5149.name: Prosecutors (US federal prosecutors)
a5149.speech: allege that Correa and other Junglers subjected victims to severe physical and mental abuse, including beatings with pipes and wires, suffocation with plastic bags, electric shocks, and dripping molten plastic or acid on detainees’ bodies. The accusations detail a harrowing campaign of violence at Gambia’s Mile 2 Prison and National Intelligence Agency headquarters, targeting political opponents during Jammeh’s 22-year dictatorship.

a5149.speaker: Pharing Sanyang, former Gambian military officer, and other survivor witnesses
a5149.name: Pharing Sanyang
a5149.title: former Gambian military officer, and other survivor witnesses
a5149.speech: Testimonies from survivors who traveled to Denver described enduring extreme cruelty at the hands of Correa and his unit.

a5149.speaker: Gambia’s Truth, Reconciliation, and Reparations Commission (TRRC) (findings)
a5149.name: Gambia’s Truth
a5149.title: Reconciliation, and Reparations Commission (TRRC) (findings)
a5149.speech: Their accounts, corroborated by findings from the TRRC, painted a grim picture of systematic torture under Jammeh’s regime.

a5149.speaker: Michael Sang Correa’s defense
a5149.name: Michael Sang Correa’s defense
a5149.speech: argued that he was a low-ranking private acting under duress, facing potential torture or death himself if he disobeyed orders.

a5149.speaker: Nicholas Westbroek, defense attorney
a5149.name: Nicholas Westbroek
a5149.title: defense attorney
a5149.speech: emphasized to jurors that “following an order is not the same as agreeing,” highlighting the climate of fear within the Junglers.

a5149.speaker: Prosecutors (US federal prosecutors)
a5149.name: Prosecutors (US federal prosecutors)
a5149.speech: countered that Correa made deliberate choices, noting that some Junglers refused to participate despite the risks, urging the jury to hold him accountable for his actions.

a5149.speaker: Human rights organizations, such as the Center for Justice and Accountability (CJA)
a5149.name: Human rights organizations
a5149.title: such as the Center for Justice and Accountability (CJA)
a5149.speech: have hailed the trial as a step toward justice for Jammeh’s victims.

a5149.speaker: Carmen Cheung Ka-Man, CJA attorney
a5149.name: Carmen Cheung Ka-Man
a5149.title: CJA attorney
a5149.speech: “This case sends a clear message: perpetrators of atrocities have nowhere to hide.”

a5149.speaker: Fatoumata Sandeng, Gambian activist whose father died in detention
a5149.name: Fatoumata Sandeng
a5149.title: Gambian activist whose father died in detention
a5149.speech: sees the trial as a complement to ongoing efforts to establish a Special Tribunal for Jammeh-era crimes, approved by ECOWAS in December 2024.

a5553.speaker: Tobie Aupindi, Swapo Party MP in the National Assembly
a5553.name: Tobie Aupindi
a5553.title: Swapo Party MP in the National Assembly
a5553.speech: Said the August House should unanimously call on the United States of America to lift the economic, financial, and commercial blockade against Cuba and its people ; added that the Assembly also urges the U.S. to immediately remove Cuba from the list of alleged state sponsors of terrorism.

a5553.speaker: Tobie Aupindi, Swapo Party MP
a5553.name: Tobie Aupindi
a5553.title: Swapo Party MP
a5553.speech: Motivating the motion, reminded MPs of the strong and historic ties between Namibia and Cuba, noting the sacrifices and support Cuba gave to Namibia during the struggle for independence.

a5553.speaker: Tobie Aupindi, Swapo Party MP
a5553.name: Tobie Aupindi
a5553.title: Swapo Party MP
a5553.speech: Pointed out that Namibia also enjoyed cooperation with the United States, particularly through programmes such as the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), which provided vital health support.

a5553.speaker: Tobie Aupindi, Swapo Party MP
a5553.name: Tobie Aupindi
a5553.title: Swapo Party MP
a5553.speech: Said tensions between the U.S. and Cuba can be traced back to the Cold War era, underlined by the Cuban Missile Crisis: "However, despite the Cold War ending some 34 years ago, the blockade on Cuba remains in place today. Today, some 63 years later, the blockade remains enforced, causing economic devastation in Cuba and great opportunities being missed by both the United States and Cuba. The current status quo is not sustainable for either country." ; stressed that the blockade caused catastrophic economic losses to the island nation, with Cuba estimated to have lost more than one trillion U.S. dollars in opportunities and growth, losses he described as unsustainable, especially for a small economy like Cuba.

a5553.speaker: Tobie Aupindi, Swapo Party MP
a5553.name: Tobie Aupindi
a5553.title: Swapo Party MP
a5553.speech: Concluded by saying Namibia stands ready to offer its mediation and play a meaningful role in promoting lasting peace, coexistence and economic opportunities between the United States and Cuba.

a5560.speaker: Shaheda Omar, clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.name: Shaheda Omar
a5560.title: clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.speech: "I think we in the NGO sector have been struggling for a long time. Unfortunately, it's not a new phenomenon, but it has become bleak. Look at the financial landscape, not only of South Africa but globally. We can see how the USAID funding has impacted so many service providers globally and, even in South Africa, where services have been shut down."

a5560.speaker: Shaheda Omar, clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.name: Shaheda Omar
a5560.title: clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.speech: Lamented the dwindling resources and its impact on collaboration among civil society organisations, noting that the competition brewing among NGOs often resulted in secrecy and a lack of unity ; "Instead of us standing united, holding hands, and trying to work together, that's not what we are finding on the ground or in practice."

a5560.speaker: Shaheda Omar, clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.name: Shaheda Omar
a5560.title: clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.speech: Shared the heart-wrenching story of a young girl impregnated twice by a teacher: "She ingested rat poison to terminate the first pregnancy and contracted HIV following the second. These are victims who are so helpless in their fight against the scourge inflicted on them."

a5560.speaker: Shaheda Omar, clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.name: Shaheda Omar
a5560.title: clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.speech: Stressed how limited funding affects the clinic's operations and the well-being of its staff: "We are overloaded. Caseloads are high, and the work comes at a price. It affects the human resources of the foundation, increasing stress levels and volumes, and there is always the risk of compassion fatigue and burnout."

a5560.speaker: Shaheda Omar, clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.name: Shaheda Omar
a5560.title: clinical director of The Teddy Bear Clinic
a5560.speech: "Every rand makes a difference in the journey to healing a child. Our mission is about promoting healing, support, and providing these children with a voice."

a5560.speaker: News24 (January report)
a5560.name: News24 (January report)
a5560.speech: Reported that the Gauteng Care Crisis Committee (GCCC) approached the courts after the department failed to comply with court orders related to the funding of NPOs.

a5560.speaker: Gauteng High Court (May 2024 order)
a5560.name: Gauteng High Court (May 2024 order)
a5560.speech: Ordered the Gauteng Department of Social Development to pay NPOs, to finalise funding applications for NPOs, issue service-level agreements, and pay NPOs within seven days of signing the agreements.

a5560.speaker: Lisa Vetten, GCCC chairperson
a5560.name: Lisa Vetten
a5560.title: GCCC chairperson
a5560.speech: Said there was a need for "accountability and transparency" regarding the funding decisions made by the department ; "The impact of funding delays on NGOs and their communities is severe, and it is urgent to resolve these issues to uphold socio-economic rights." ; said some organisations faced closure "with reports of suicides due to lack of services" ; "There are firm deadlines to settle these outstanding issues as the end of the financial year approaches."

a5621.speaker: Ban Ki-Moon, UN Secretary-General (anniversary message)
a5621.name: Ban Ki-Moon
a5621.title: UN Secretary-General (anniversary message)
a5621.speech: "At 70, the UN can look back on a proud record, that of having worked with many partners to eliminate colonialism, defeat apartheid, maintain peace in troubled places and craft a body of treaties and rights to protect human rights. Every day, the UN feeds people suffering from hunger, shelters refugees and vaccinates children against polio and other deadly diseases. Our humanitarian workers brave remote and dangerous environments to deliver humanitarian aid, and our mediators strive to find common ground between warring parties and peaceful solutions to grievances and disputes."

a5621.speaker: Rosine Sori Coulibaly, Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.name: Rosine Sori Coulibaly
a5621.title: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.speech: Said the institution was born out of the chaos and devastation of the Second World War, and added that its mission has always remained guided by its charter, which orients its interventions in the pillar areas of peace, sustainable development and human rights.

a5621.speaker: Rosine Sori Coulibaly, Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.name: Rosine Sori Coulibaly
a5621.title: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.speech: Stated that the UN is today at a turning point in its history with the adoption, on 25 September, of the new sustainable development agenda for 2030, comprising 17 Sustainable Development Goals broken down into 189 targets.

a5621.speaker: Rosine Sori Coulibaly, Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.name: Rosine Sori Coulibaly
a5621.title: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.speech: "Since Benin's independence, the United Nations has supported the country in its development process by providing substantial material aid, but also technical assistance" ; said that since 1990 great progress has been made with the support of the United Nations and all development partners: gender parity between girls and boys in primary education is close to being achieved, polio has been eradicated, and the proportion of the population suffering from hunger has been halved.

a5621.speaker: Rosine Sori Coulibaly, Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.name: Rosine Sori Coulibaly
a5621.title: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.speech: Noted that for the 2014-2018 period the United Nations will provide Benin with substantial financial and technical support of nearly 970 million US dollars: "Beyond this material aid, we place at the disposal of Benin's institutions and people our expertise in six areas of intervention: inclusive growth, employment, food security, gender equality and social protection, health including HIV/AIDS, non-communicable diseases, nutrition, family planning, basic sanitation, basic education, protection against social vulnerability, violence and abuse, governance, and decentralisation, and finally the environment, the management of crises and disasters, and climate change."

a5621.speaker: Rosine Sori Coulibaly, Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.name: Rosine Sori Coulibaly
a5621.title: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5621.speech: Stressed that all resident and non-resident agencies operating in Benin are now working to make Benin a flagship country in the implementation of the UN reform known as "Delivering as One" ; "This reform aims to strengthen the coherence and synergy of the international organisation's actions in order to rationalise costs while guaranteeing the quality of interventions for the benefit of the people."

a5621.speaker: Saliou Akadiri, Beninese Minister in charge of Foreign Affairs
a5621.name: Saliou Akadiri
a5621.title: Beninese Minister in charge of Foreign Affairs
a5621.speech: Wished the institution a happy anniversary and noted that the 55 years of UN presence in Benin are a sign of the country's attachment to its values: "It is an occasion to reaffirm the values and successes of the Organisation and to recall the many challenges it faces." He further assured the institution of the constant availability of the services of the Beninese administration for the accomplishment of its mission.

a5657.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Senegalese Prime Minister
a5657.name: Ousmane Sonko
a5657.title: Senegalese Prime Minister
a5657.speech: Declared on Monday at Fass Touré, in the Louga region, that the suspension of official development assistance announced by the President of the United States concerns an electrification programme implemented in Senegal with 318 billion CFA francs of financing from the American government: “We cannot continue to depend on foreign aid. The day before yesterday, the new American president announced a suspension of all United States development aid programmes for poor countries, for a period of three [months], pending a decision on what he will do with them” ; “One of the suspended financings was destined for an electrification programme implemented in Senegal. It is a financing of 500 million US dollars (318 billion CFA francs at the current dollar exchange rate).”

a5657.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Senegalese Prime Minister
a5657.name: Ousmane Sonko
a5657.title: Senegalese Prime Minister
a5657.speech: Invited his compatriots to work hard so as no longer to depend on aid provided by developed countries: “Should we continue to depend on foreign aid? We must work hard to implement our own programmes. If we do that, we will be cited, in the years to come, among the best-managed countries.”

a5725.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Djiboutian Minister of National Education and Vocational Training
a5725.name: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud
a5725.title: Djiboutian Minister of National Education and Vocational Training
a5725.speech: Contributed substantially to the discussions on funding allocations and on the GPE's financing strategy for 2025-2030, and also shared Djibouti's education policies as defined by President Ismail Omar Guelleh and the results of the “citizen school”, as well as the transformations under way, notably the integrated rural school.

a5725.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Djiboutian Minister of National Education and Vocational Training
a5725.name: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud
a5725.title: Djiboutian Minister of National Education and Vocational Training
a5725.speech: As guest of honour at the event celebrating the International Day of Play, shared Djibouti's experience in pre-school education based on play-based pedagogy, supported by USAID Djibouti.

a5746.speaker: Ministries and agencies appearing before the Liberian Senate
a5746.name: Ministries and agencies appearing before the Liberian Senate
a5746.speech: Provided information to the Senate on the current status of the situation and their respective ideas for the way forward.

a5746.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a5746.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a5746.title: Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a5746.speech: Informed the Liberian Senate that the Ministry was analyzing and documenting how the USAID shutdown is impacting the country; said the Ministry was preparing for all eventualities beyond the three months which the US government indicated was the timeframe for the USAID suspension, costing Liberia $118 in loss; said the impact of the cut affects several government institutions that include Health, Education, Elections, and Domestic revenue mobilization, prayerful that other projects may not be affected in the coming days or weeks.

a5746.speaker: Senators Amara Konneh (Gbarpolu), Gbezohngar Findley (Grand Bassa), Abraham Darius Dillon (Montserrado) and Augustine Chea (Sinoe) (joint communication)
a5746.name: Senators Amara Konneh (Gbarpolu)
a5746.title: Gbezohngar Findley (Grand Bassa), Abraham Darius Dillon (Montserrado) and Augustine Chea (Sinoe) (joint communication)
a5746.speech: Collectively emphasized the urgent need for the Liberian government to reassess its budgeting and to develop financing strategies due to the possible disruption of USAID-funded initiatives.

a5746.speaker: Trump administration
a5746.name: Trump administration
a5746.speech: Cited the need to realign USAID's efforts with the "America First" agenda in cancelling and/or freezing all projects worldwide for a period of 90 days.

a5746.speaker: Liberian Senate hearings chaired by Grand Cape Mount County Senator Debah Varpilah
a5746.name: Liberian Senate hearings chaired by Grand Cape Mount County Senator Debah Varpilah
a5746.speech: Were used to ask the Finance Ministry in particular to provide a full detailed analysis report that will inform the Senate on the next course of action; the Ministries of Education and Health have also been cited to return and provide more information on the situation, with the Health Minister proper, not deputies, asked to form part of the hearing.

a5773.speaker: Council of the Arab League (closing session resolutions)
a5773.name: Council of the Arab League (closing session resolutions)
a5773.speech: Renewed its call to protect the Palestinian people from genocide, displacement and ethnic cleansing and to prevent the liquidation of its central cause, on the basis of resolutions of international legitimacy, international law and relevant agreements, including Security Council resolutions 904 (1994) and 605 (1987), General Assembly resolution 20/10 (2018) and the Treaty of Joint Defence and Economic Cooperation between member states of the Arab League, while guaranteeing the protection of member states’ interests, sovereign decisions and legal obligations.

a5773.speaker: Council of the Arab League
a5773.name: Council of the Arab League
a5773.speech: Condemned the decisions and plans of the Israeli government to continue the occupation of the Gaza Strip and to displace the population, considering them a violation of international law, a flagrant aggression against the national security and interests of the Arab countries and a threat to peace and stability in the region; stressed the need to implement the decisions of the joint Arab and Arab-Islamic summits in order to break the Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip and to force the entry of humanitarian aid by land, sea and air in cooperation with the United Nations and its organisations, including UNRWA.

a5773.speaker: Council of the Arab League
a5773.name: Council of the Arab League
a5773.speech: Called on the two Arab members of the Security Council (Algeria and Somalia) and the Arab Group in New York to continue their efforts to end the Israeli aggression, including submitting a draft resolution under Chapter VII obliging the occupying power to a ceasefire, allowing the import of aid and ending the occupation, and imposing international sanctions on it; states should also be called upon to take legal and administrative measures, including preventing the export, transfer or transit of weapons, ammunition and military material to Israel, reviewing economic relations with Israel, and initiating investigations and prosecutions against Israeli officials.

a5773.speaker: Council of the Arab League
a5773.name: Council of the Arab League
a5773.speech: Called on civil society and human rights organisations to track down and hold accountable those involved in Israeli war crimes; emphasised the empowerment of the State of Palestine to assume full governmental responsibility in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, within the framework of the political programme of the Palestine Liberation Organisation.

a5773.speaker: Council of the Arab League
a5773.name: Council of the Arab League
a5773.speech: Condemned Israel’s use of starvation as a means of genocide, in which 200 Palestinian civilians, half of them children, died, and stated that the “death traps” set up by the occupation forces under the cover of the so-called “Gaza Humanitarian Foundation” claimed 1,500 martyrs and thousands of wounded; held Israel fully responsible for the blockade and its consequences.

a5773.speaker: Council of the Arab League
a5773.name: Council of the Arab League
a5773.speech: Stressed the boycott of companies that contribute to strengthening the occupation economy or support the crimes of genocide and ethnic cleansing, especially those mentioned in the reports of the Human Rights Council and the UN Special Rapporteur; reaffirmed the implementation of Security Council resolutions 2735, 2712 and 2720 concerning the ceasefire, the return of the displaced, the distribution of aid, the exchange of prisoners and the complete withdrawal from the Gaza Strip; welcomed the international positions rejecting Israeli military control over Gaza and the annexation of the West Bank; confirmed the continuation of the Council session and instructed the Secretary-General to monitor the implementation of the resolutions and submit a report to the next session.

a5773.speaker: Muhannad Al-Aklouk, Palestinian delegate to the Arab League (ambassador)
a5773.name: Muhannad Al-Aklouk
a5773.title: Palestinian delegate to the Arab League (ambassador)
a5773.speech: Stressed how important it is to continue and intensify international efforts to end the war of extermination and starvation against the Palestinian people and to thwart the occupying power’s plans to bring Gaza under its control and annex the West Bank; stated that the Council unanimously approved the Palestinian draft resolution to end the war and immediately deliver aid, and emphasised: “Israel is slaughtering the humanity of the world, and Palestine is the scene of this crime.”

a5773.speaker: Muhannad Al-Aklouk, Palestinian delegate to the Arab League (ambassador)
a5773.name: Muhannad Al-Aklouk
a5773.title: Palestinian delegate to the Arab League (ambassador)
a5773.speech: Pointed out that the occupying power has killed and injured more than a quarter of a million Palestinians, including 18,500 children, and starved more than 200 civilians to death, half of them children; added that the occupying power’s plans aim to repeat the Nakba of 1948 through new forced displacements, since the Israeli parliament has approved the annexation of the occupied West Bank and prevented the establishment of a Palestinian state there.

a6044.speaker: Cllr. Sylvester D. Rennie, President of the Liberian National Bar Association (LNBA)
a6044.name: Cllr. Sylvester D. Rennie
a6044.title: President of the Liberian National Bar Association (LNBA)
a6044.speech: Said at least 71% of inmates languishing behind bars in Liberia are pretrial detainees: “Even those who commit non-bailable crimes are also incarcerated. It has been observed that most of these detainees at our various prison facilities in Liberia are pre-trial detainees, which constitute 71% of the overall number of detainees in the Country” ; said that when these offenders are arrested and taken to the law, in most instances, they are unable to meet the needed provisions to secure their release and are therefore incarcerated.

a6044.speaker: Cllr. Sylvester D. Rennie, President of the Liberian National Bar Association (LNBA)
a6044.name: Cllr. Sylvester D. Rennie
a6044.title: President of the Liberian National Bar Association (LNBA)
a6044.speech: Giving an overview of what prompted the programme's implementation and partnership, said the LNBA has realized that crimes are committed daily, violating the law: “As a means of having some of our prisons decongested, the LNBA and the UNDP with funding from the International Narcotics & Law Enforcement (INL) signed a grant agreement for the decongestion of pretrial detainees at the Monrovia Central Prison. This process is for one year, and it is also being launched. We want to thank the UNDP and the INL for this collaboration.”

a6044.speaker: Cllr. Frederick L. M. Gbemie, Project Manager
a6044.name: Cllr. Frederick L. M. Gbemie
a6044.title: Project Manager
a6044.speech: Said that the project's goal is to sensitize, encourage, and promote legal protection for vulnerable and indigent citizens through the provision of pro bono legal aid services for the most egregious cases by members of the LNBA as an alternate condition for renewal of practicing licenses ; indicated that by this intervention, the LNBA seeks to sensitize and encourage members of the LNBA to provide pro bono legal aid as one of the alternate conditions for the renewal of practicing licenses: “The LNBA will Provide legal aid services for the most egregious cases to reduce docket overcrowding and pre-trial detention in Montserrado county and educate citizens on how to access the LNBA Pro Bono Legal Aid Services and encourage indigents to take advantage of the opportunity to access justice. To successfully make the above intervention, the LNBA Action would be to hold one day of LNBA stakeholders' clarity and brainstorming meetings” ; stated that the launch of the project holds a one-day LNBA Legal Aid National Symposium, produce and publicize Pro-Bono/Free Legal Aid Service awareness materials such as drama, jingles, and stickers.

a6092.speaker: Prof Oatlhokwa Nkomazana, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Health (Botswana)
a6092.name: Prof Oatlhokwa Nkomazana
a6092.title: Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Health (Botswana)
a6092.speech: said the projects were carefully designed to provide complementary support to the government's critical priorities in the areas of orphans and vulnerable children (OVC). She added that their collective goal was to end HIV as a public health threat by 2030 by demonstrating global best practices in health and revitalising primary health care in the country.

a6092.speaker: Prof Oatlhokwa Nkomazana, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Health (Botswana)
a6092.name: Prof Oatlhokwa Nkomazana
a6092.title: Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Health (Botswana)
a6092.speech: "The Ministry congratulates the three organisations; Stepping Stones International, Tebelopele Wellness Centre and Jhpiego on being selected to implement these transformative programmes to strengthen our HIV response as a country. We sincerely appreciate the U.S. government's unwavering dedication to supporting Botswana's health initiatives."

a6092.speaker: Prof Oatlhokwa Nkomazana, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Health (Botswana)
a6092.name: Prof Oatlhokwa Nkomazana
a6092.title: Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Health (Botswana)
a6092.speech: "Our government has made significant strides in the global HIV response, being a global leader in the fight against HIV/AIDS. Today, the country has one of the highest rates of viral suppression in the world and has achieved the UNAIDS 2030 fast-track targets of 95-95-95 by reaching an impressive 95-98-98." ; further stated that despite that monumental achievement, their work was by no means over adding that they had a collective responsibility to reach all populations and leaving no one behind, especially the remaining 5-2-2 populations. She also said they had to continue to innovate and expand their services to address those gaps. She added that their focus must be on elevating the quality of life for all and sustaining the gains by maintaining a country-owned, sustainable direction that leaves no one behind.

a6191.speaker: Army General Assimi Goita, President of the AES Confederation
a6191.name: Army General Assimi Goita
a6191.title: President of the AES Confederation
a6191.speech: Read out a sober and solemn communique on 4 July 2025 to announce the holding this coming December, in the Malian capital, of the second session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation.

a6191.speaker: Alfousseini Sanou, Malian Minister of Economy and Finance
a6191.name: Alfousseini Sanou
a6191.title: Malian Minister of Economy and Finance
a6191.speech: Announced on Friday 23 May 2025 the operationalisation of the AES Confederal Investment and Development Bank (BCID-AES).

a6191.speaker: Dr Aboubacar Nacanabo, Burkinabe Minister of Economy
a6191.name: Dr Aboubacar Nacanabo
a6191.title: Burkinabe Minister of Economy
a6191.speech: According to him, the BCID, a genuine financial arm of the organisation, is an initiative that carries hope.

a6191.speaker: Alliance of Sahel States (AES)
a6191.name: Alliance of Sahel States (AES)
a6191.speech: Announced on 11 July 2025 the creation of a Criminal and Human Rights Court (CPS-DH) in Bamako, to be tasked with trying war crimes, crimes against humanity, terrorism and serious human rights violations, with a high-security prison and a digital platform for judicial cooperation.

a6191.speaker: AES Ministers in charge of Communication
a6191.name: AES Ministers in charge of Communication
a6191.speech: Unveiled the logo and the digital platform including an AES WebTV at the end of the AES communication and ICT experts' workshop held from 27 to 29 December 2024 in Bamako; the Confederation's motto "One Space - One People - One Destiny" was unveiled at the same time as its logo.

a6191.speaker: AES Humanitarian Forum, Bamako Declaration (first edition, 7-9 August 2025)
a6191.name: AES Humanitarian Forum
a6191.title: Bamako Declaration (first edition, 7-9 August 2025)
a6191.speech: Resulted in the Bamako Declaration and in the establishment of a consultation framework for sovereign and effective humanitarian action, aimed at reducing dependence on foreign aid and aligning actions with national priorities.

a6233.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a6233.name: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud
a6233.title: Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a6233.speech: In his opening remarks to the workshop, highlighted the priorities of the current Education Action Plan (PAE), organised around five areas, including increasing access to one year of pre-school by 2020, strengthening equity for inclusive education, and improving the quality of learning.

a6233.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a6233.name: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud
a6233.title: Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a6233.speech: Expressed his sincere thanks and congratulated all the participants in the work, paying tribute to the participation of the partners, which is valuable support in implementing the MENFOP's policy, and welcoming the sincerity and the well-coordinated work that makes it possible to benefit from financial as well as technical support and expertise.

a6233.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a6233.name: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud
a6233.title: Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a6233.speech: "The PAE will be strengthened by new projects financed by the World Bank under the transformative project for national education and vocational training and by the USAID reading support project. The greatest challenge for the ministry at present is that of access to school for all. In line with the government's political will, we intend to allow the greatest number of Djiboutian children - all children, I should say - to have access to school whatever their place of residence, whatever the difficulties linked to their disability or their social status, targeting mainly the most remote and most isolated corners of the country where unfortunately there are still a good number of children outside the education system. We simply aim to enrol all Djiboutian children within a few years, as well as those of so-called floating families present on national soil, because every child has the right to schooling and none must be left on the margins."

a6233.speaker: Djanabou Mahonde, UNICEF Representative in Djibouti and head of the local education partners group
a6233.name: Djanabou Mahonde
a6233.title: UNICEF Representative in Djibouti and head of the local education partners group
a6233.speech: Echoed the MENFOP and recalled the objectives of the meeting, which should make it possible "to assess the progress made during 2018 in the implementation of the PAE 2017/2020, to identify the challenges, and to formulate relevant recommendations."

a6233.speaker: Djanabou Mahonde, UNICEF Representative in Djibouti and head of the local education partners group
a6233.name: Djanabou Mahonde
a6233.title: UNICEF Representative in Djibouti and head of the local education partners group
a6233.speech: "UNICEF, in its capacity as head of the local education partners, welcomes the excellent collaboration that exists between the MENFOP and the sector's technical and financial partners. The sectoral coordination platform is of paramount importance in ensuring that partners' interventions are aligned with the strategic priorities of the Government of Djibouti for access to quality education for all girls and boys living on Djiboutian territory. The second annual review of the education action plan (PAE) 2017-2020 made it possible to assess the progress under way and to identify together solutions to meet the challenges and propose corrective actions. The particularity of this year's review was the bilateral consultations and joint visits that preceded the work itself. The presentation of the first results of the study on out-of-school children highlighted the situation of children in rural areas, particularly girls, those living in Djibouti, street children, refugee children and also those living with a disability. The results will make it possible to identify strategies and interventions adapted to the realities of each group in order to integrate them effectively into the education system and thus ensure their schooling. I reiterate here the commitment of the local education partners to work alongside the Government of Djibouti through the MENFOP to achieve the results of the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 4, which focuses on equitable access to quality education."

a6233.speaker: Barbara Manzi, Coordinator of the United Nations system in Djibouti
a6233.name: Barbara Manzi
a6233.title: Coordinator of the United Nations system in Djibouti
a6233.speech: Similar echoes were heard in her remarks, alongside those of the UNICEF representative and head of the local education partners group, thanking and paying tribute to the partners and participants.

a6233.speaker: Study on out-of-school children (presented at the review)
a6233.name: Study on out-of-school children (presented at the review)
a6233.speech: Its first results highlighted the situation of children in rural areas, particularly girls, children living in Djibouti city, street children, refugee children and children living with a disability.

a6233.speaker: Thematic working groups of the review (synthesis of recommendations)
a6233.name: Thematic working groups of the review (synthesis of recommendations)
a6233.speech: Recommended, for pre-school education, increasing provision by strengthening reception facilities and recruiting teachers; for basic education, strengthening rural schooling through incentives such as school transport and dormitories for girls; for lower and upper secondary education, combating school drop-out through a dedicated strategy, mentoring follow-up and targeted guidance discussed with parents; for technical and vocational education and training (TVET), accelerating the promulgation of the national policy and the drafting of the operational action plan, expanding reception facilities, strengthening administrative and teaching teams and involving the private sector; and, for sectoral monitoring, making the corresponding financial statements available to the directorates-general on the basis of the three-year budgeted activity plan and providing the CFEEF with training needs so as to design the three-year training plan through a participatory approach.

a6251.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a6251.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a6251.speech: Welcomes a generous contribution of EUR 500,000 from the Government of Finland to provide tens of thousands of children with daily hot meals as part of Mozambique's ongoing National Home-Grown School Feeding Programme (PRONAE).

a6251.speaker: Satu Lassila, Ambassador of Finland to Mozambique
a6251.name: Satu Lassila
a6251.title: Ambassador of Finland to Mozambique
a6251.speech: “School meals are more than just a plate of food; they are a vital investment in the future of Mozambican children” ; “Finland has a long-standing partnership with Mozambique, including in education. I am delighted that we can now support Mozambican children also in this way.”

a6251.speaker: Antonella D'Aprile, WFP Country Director in Mozambique
a6251.name: Antonella D'Aprile
a6251.title: WFP Country Director in Mozambique
a6251.speech: “Investing in school meals is one of the smartest and most impactful ways to support the next generations in Mozambique” ; “Thanks to Finland's generous contribution, thousands of children will receive the nourishment they need to learn and build a better future—not only for themselves but for the country as a whole.”

a6251.speaker: WFP Mozambique (@wfp_mozambique) (social media post)
a6251.name: WFP Mozambique (@wfp_mozambique) (social media post)
a6251.speech: “Thanks to a generous contribution from #Finland, 56K children in northern #Mozambique will receive daily #schoolmeals for 3 months. This boost to the national programme #PRONAE is an investment in the future of children.”

a6398.speaker: Loide Kasingo, Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a6398.name: Loide Kasingo
a6398.title: Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a6398.speech: Has called on all African countries to introduce national programmes aimed at educating young people on the ideals of Pan-Africanism to strengthen unity and promote development on the continent ; said this is especially important to ensure that young people, “who are the leaders of tomorrow”, understand the importance of Pan-Africanism for development ; said “the revival of Pan-Africanism is essential for us to develop”, because citizens of the continent, including leaders, seem to have lost the values and ideals of Pan-Africanism ; “In Namibia, Pan-Africanism is lacking, especially among the youth. They do not understand what Pan-Africanism is all about, and therefore do not live up to its spirit. Many young people today focus on getting rich quickly, disregarding the spirit of sharing to ensure everyone has bread on their table” ; “Young people need to be educated about the AU and its associated institutions. This would ensure that future leaders understand and embody the spirit of Pan-Africanism.”

a6398.speaker: Loide Kasingo, Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a6398.name: Loide Kasingo
a6398.title: Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a6398.speech: Credited Founding President Sam Nujoma as a key advocate for the establishment of AU's legislative body ; proposed that future members of PAP undergo assessments to ensure they truly understand Pan-Africanism.

a6398.speaker: Loide Kasingo, Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a6398.name: Loide Kasingo
a6398.title: Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a6398.speech: Emphasised the need for African countries to reduce their dependence on foreign aid, and focus on self-funding to spur genuine development across the continent. “If we don't fund ourselves, we will keep on begging from others, although our continent is very rich,” she stated ; addressing the AU's funding challenges, proposed the idea of an AU levy on resources like diamonds and oil, suggesting these funds support AU operations, including PAP: “Maybe we should collect the levy from those harvesting our resources. Such a levy could then fund AU's budget, and support PAP's work” ; expressed concern that while Africa is rich in resources, its people remain poor due to mismanagement and external exploitation: “Africa, as a continent, is rich, but its people are poor. We often choose to study abroad, rather than investing in our own institutions at home. This shows that we have yet to decolonise our minds.”

a6398.speaker: Chief Fortune Charumbira, President of the Pan-African Parliament (PAP)
a6398.name: Chief Fortune Charumbira
a6398.title: President of the Pan-African Parliament (PAP)
a6398.speech: In his opening remarks, said the parliament's strategic plan is designed to deepen Africa's economic integration, democratic governance, and stability. “This strategic plan is our collective vision, crafted through extensive consultations with our stakeholders,” he remarked ; noted that the parliament consulted with representatives from African Union institutions, civil society, and regional bodies to shape the vision of a united and empowered Africa ; “The Pan-African parliament is not just another institution. It is the legislative voice of Africa, committed to fully involving our people in building the Africa we aspire for,” he stated ; emphasised PAP's mission to be the guardian of African citizens' aspirations; highlighted the goal of enabling PAP to effectively fulfil its legislative and oversight roles, while championing human rights, economic integration and good governance; and urged the parliament to commit to transparency and inclusivity, ensuring the strategy reflects Africa's achievements and challenges alike.

a6398.speaker: Djiddar Mamar, fourth vice president of the Pan-African Parliament
a6398.name: Djiddar Mamar
a6398.title: fourth vice president of the Pan-African Parliament
a6398.speech: In his welcoming remarks, called the workshop “a crucial endeavour for the Pan-African Parliament and Africa”.

a6460.speaker: National Agricultural Marketing Board (NAMBoard) (notice/statement)
a6460.name: National Agricultural Marketing Board (NAMBoard) (notice/statement)
a6460.speech: Announced a new trade restriction placing a total ban on the importation of sugar beans into the Kingdom of Eswatini, taking effect on September 22, 2025, following a recent assessment that found local bean production has now surpassed national demand ; highlighted that the country has witnessed a significant rise in the production of sugar beans, one of the staple commodities also supported by the NMC ; “After an assessment of the situation by the Ministry of Agriculture, NMC and NAMBoard, it has been established that local bean production has increased beyond the national demand,” the notice reads ; confirmed that the restriction is not permanent and will be reviewed if domestic supply falls short of market needs.

a6460.speaker: NAMBoard officials
a6460.name: NAMBoard officials
a6460.speech: Argue that with greater support from government initiatives, development partners, and private sector investment, local farmers are producing more than enough to meet national consumption needs ; say the move will also reduce the risk of oversupply, which often drives down farm-gate prices, leaving farmers unable to cover production costs ; state that sugar bean yields now comfortably exceed what the domestic market requires.

a6460.speaker: NAMBoard (assurances to consumers)
a6460.name: NAMBoard (assurances to consumers)
a6460.speech: Assured consumers that close monitoring will be conducted to avoid any gaps in the market, and that if local supplies drop below required thresholds, restrictions will be lifted or adjusted to prevent shortages ; insists that it will maintain a balance, prioritising the protection of farmers while ensuring that consumers are not disadvantaged ; concluded its statement by assuring the public that monitoring will be continuous and that any changes in production or supply levels will trigger a review of the restriction.

a6460.speaker: NAMBoard (statement)
a6460.name: NAMBoard (statement)
a6460.speech: “For any enquiries regarding the above-mentioned notice, please contact the Head of Legal, Trade and Regulation, Bongani Mdluli, at 7802 2963,” the statement said.

a6460.speaker: NAMBoard (report on earlier restrictions)
a6460.name: NAMBoard (report on earlier restrictions)
a6460.speech: Has reported that the earlier tomato and beetroot restrictions did not lead to shortages, as local farmers were quick to fill the supply gap.

a6660.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.name: Muhammad Pate
a6660.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.speech: Disclosed after the FEC meeting on Wednesday that the Federal Executive Council approved contracts of N10.3 billion for the procurement of essential medical supplies, and noted that the approval is aimed at enhancing the accessibility and affordability of health commodities and health services by Nigerians.

a6660.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.name: Muhammad Pate
a6660.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.speech: On HIV drugs: "A few weeks ago, we approved the first-line antiretroviral drugs, and now we are putting forth resources, almost N997 million worth of contract, to procure the third-line antiretroviral drugs for those who are HIV-infected." ; noted the significance of this procurement in ensuring that Nigerians living with HIV continue to receive uninterrupted treatment despite changes in international health aid.

a6660.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.name: Muhammad Pate
a6660.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.speech: On diabetes: "Diabetes is a major issue in our country. It's among the fastest-growing segments. We have lots of our population suffering from diabetes, and some are not even aware they have it." ; noted that for the first time a Nigerian company based in Lagos will manufacture the diagnostic kits: "So government is procuring the diagnostic kits the on point blood glucose monitoring system that is manufactured here in Nigeria. This is bringing to life the effort to unlock the healthcare value chain by encouraging local manufacturers."

a6660.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.name: Muhammad Pate
a6660.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.speech: On the N4.5 billion medical relief programme: "These are also commodities that are manufactured by local manufacturers here in Nigeria, so we are beginning to pool the demand and patronise our local manufacturers."

a6660.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.name: Muhammad Pate
a6660.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.speech: On hospital equipment: "The Federal Executive Council approved the procurement of a mobile X-ray machine and also the rehabilitation and equipping of a computerised tomography CAT scan, a 64-slice CT scan, for that teaching hospital." ; added that the approvals reflect the Tinubu administration's ongoing efforts to transform Nigeria's healthcare system by increasing domestic financing, supporting local production and improving healthcare infrastructure.

a6660.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.name: Muhammad Pate
a6660.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6660.speech: Reassured stakeholders that the Nigerian government is proactively developing a transition and sustainability plan to address potential funding shortfalls, and said the government has set up a multi-ministerial committee including representatives from the Ministries of Finance, Health, Defence and Environment as well as the Governors' Forum: "This is to ensure that Nigerians receiving treatment do not face disruptions."

a6730.speaker: UN Security Council (press statement)
a6730.name: UN Security Council (press statement)
a6730.speech: The council urged Rwanda and the DRC to return to talks to achieve peace and address issues related to the presence of Rwanda Defence Forces in the eastern Congo and Congolese support for the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR).

a6730.speaker: UN Security Council (press statement)
a6730.name: UN Security Council (press statement)
a6730.speech: “condemned the ongoing flagrant disregard for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, including the unauthorized presence in the Eastern DRC of external forces” ; It did not explicitly name the external forces but demanded that they “withdraw immediately.”

a6730.speaker: UN Security Council (press statement)
a6730.name: UN Security Council (press statement)
a6730.speech: “The members of the Security Council are also deeply alarmed by continued occurrences of GPS jamming and spoofing activities in support of M23 operations in North Kivu, which represent imminent risk to civil aviation safety and negatively impact the delivery of humanitarian assistance to populations in need,” the Security Council said.

a6730.speaker: M23
a6730.name: M23
a6730.speech: M23 vows to defend Tutsi interests, particularly against ethnic Hutu militias such as the FDLR.

a6730.speaker: United States, France and Britain
a6730.name: United States
a6730.title: France and Britain
a6730.speech: At the council meeting on Sunday, the United States, France and Britain condemned what they said was Rwanda’s backing of the M23 rebel advance.

a6730.speaker: Kigali (Rwandan government)
a6730.name: Kigali (Rwandan government)
a6730.speech: Kigali has long denied supporting M23.

a6730.speaker: Dorothy Shea, Acting U.S. Ambassador to the U.N.
a6730.name: Dorothy Shea
a6730.title: Acting U.S. Ambassador to the U.N.
a6730.speech: specifically called out Rwanda for using GPS jamming and spoofing, which was also reflected in the council statement.

a6730.speaker: UN Report (@UN_Report), social media post
a6730.name: UN Report (@UN_Report)
a6730.title: social media post
a6730.speech: “#UNSC issues a press statement on the situation in the #DRC, penned by @franceonu. See agreed text below.”

a6830.speaker: Jacinto Veloso, member of Mozambique’s National Defence and Security Council (CNDS), former Security Minister (writing in Savana, 5 June)
a6830.name: Jacinto Veloso
a6830.title: member of Mozambique’s National Defence and Security Council (CNDS), former Security Minister (writing in Savana, 5 June)
a6830.speech: “I am convinced that we are facing a major operation whose objective is to block the natural gas projects of Cabo Delgado” ; “We are confronted with a mega-operation of destabilisation very probably directed by a competent and powerful hub located somewhere outside the country.” ; “We are dealing with a mega-operation conceived, directed, and executed from outside the country to, at least, slow the natural gas projects, because they are considered a serious commercial threat to the giant economic interests of big companies involved in identical projects in the region which are competing for the same markets.”

a6830.speaker: Jacinto Veloso, member of Mozambique’s National Defence and Security Council (CNDS)
a6830.name: Jacinto Veloso
a6830.title: member of Mozambique’s National Defence and Security Council (CNDS)
a6830.speech: Cites as a model the United States use of Islamic fundamentalists, notably Osama bin Laden, in Afghanistan from 1979 to eventually defeat the Russians; argues that Mozambique is confronting Islamic State, not local insurgents; and argues that to respond, “prompt external help is inevitable.” He does not say which competing gas producers are using Islamic State.

a6830.speaker: Jacinto Veloso, member of Mozambique’s National Defence and Security Council (CNDS)
a6830.name: Jacinto Veloso
a6830.title: member of Mozambique’s National Defence and Security Council (CNDS)
a6830.speech: Explicitly dismisses the idea that this is an internal war based on “local discontents”, and rejects the views of journalists and academics who argue this is mainly a domestic insurgency.

a6830.speaker: Jasmine Opperman (@Jasminechic00), analyst (Twitter post, 6 June 2020)
a6830.name: Jasmine Opperman (@Jasminechic00)
a6830.title: analyst (Twitter post, 6 June 2020)
a6830.speech: “This is a question constantly raised in our team: Considering the hypothesis of sabotage of LNG projects, General Jacinto Veloso raised in the latest edition of Jornal Savana, it is appropriate to ask why the Palma district is relatively free from attacks?”

a6830.speaker: Hilary Matfess and Alexander Noyes, Rand Corporation (4 June article, World Politics Review)
a6830.name: Hilary Matfess and Alexander Noyes
a6830.title: Rand Corporation (4 June article, World Politics Review)
a6830.speech: “Despite … purported international links, the existing evidence suggests that the insurgency should be considered primarily an outgrowth of local economic and political conditions” ; they stress that “compared to other provinces, Cabo Delgado is impoverished and its residents lack access to health and education services. The Islamists’ propaganda has capitalised on these disparities, emphasising the insurgents’ local connections.” They stress the similarities to Boko Haram in Nigeria.

a6830.speaker: Hilary Matfess and Alexander Noyes, Rand Corporation (1 September 2019 article in Lawfare)
a6830.name: Hilary Matfess and Alexander Noyes
a6830.title: Rand Corporation (1 September 2019 article in Lawfare)
a6830.speech: “The experience of other African countries provides an instructive lesson: A hardline response that depends solely on repression will only make things worse. Mozambique needs to handle this growing security challenge in a way that will tackle the problem instead of exacerbating it with heavy-handed tactics justified as being ‘tough on terrorism.’ A more comprehensive approach, which focuses on shared socioeconomic development and leverages international partnerships, would be more effective.” There is a need “to fairly distribute wealth from the natural gas boom. Impoverished northern Mozambique needs development-focused efforts in particular. … Repression will only make things worse.”

a6830.speaker: Media Bias/Fact Check (mediabiasfactcheck.com)
a6830.name: Media Bias/Fact Check (mediabiasfactcheck.com)
a6830.speech: Rates the journal World Politics Review as one of the “least biased” and “most credible” media sources.

a6830.speaker: Rural residents of northern Mozambique (people interviewed by the author, anonymous)
a6830.name: Rural residents of northern Mozambique (people interviewed by the author
a6830.title: anonymous)
a6830.speech: A common refrain — “my children may go to school, but my wallet is still empty” — and they see an elite whose wallets are not empty and who appear to be growing fat.

a6830.speaker: Joseph Hanlon, Civil War, Civil Peace (textbook)
a6830.name: Joseph Hanlon
a6830.title: Civil War, Civil Peace (textbook)
a6830.speech: Underlined that while nearly all civil wars have some outside involvement, they also are based on local grievances.

a6830.speaker: Pseudonymous researcher, paper published by CMI (Chr Michelsen Institute), 27 May
a6830.name: Pseudonymous researcher
a6830.title: paper published by CMI (Chr Michelsen Institute), 27 May
a6830.speech: Argues that “The Nyusi government would need to heed the call by civil society and its leaders, including those of faith-based groups, to stop pursuing a military ‘solution’ to the conflict and to relinquish and ban any external support, i.e. the internationalisation of the war”; warns that if the war continues to escalate, “The simmering political, ethnic and religious wounds, old and new, would certainly break open and not only divide Cabo Delgado, but possibly the whole country in form of a civil war.”

a6830.speaker: CMI (Chr Michelsen Institute) paper
a6830.name: CMI (Chr Michelsen Institute) paper
a6830.speech: Notes that “It is certainly true that the seeds of Wahabism [were] planted in Cabo Delgado, particularly in the 1980s by the Islamic Council of Mozambique (CISLAMO) and its leaders. … There is a historical link of Wahabi-oriented CISLAMO to the business community in northern Mozambique, mostly composed of Mozambican non-African businesspeople usually of Indian or Pakistani origin, colloquially and derogatorily referred to as monhés. Many of them are intrinsically linked to and support the Frelimo party, which, even at senior leadership level not only ignores this group’s involvement in illicit trade, e.g. heroin via the coast of Cabo Delgado and Nampula, but benefit directly from it.”

a6830.speaker: CMI (Chr Michelsen Institute) paper
a6830.name: CMI (Chr Michelsen Institute) paper
a6830.speech: Argues that the Cabo Delgado civil war fits into Prof Mary Kaldor’s 2005 concept of “new wars” in which the parties gain not from victory but from the on-going fighting, through trade, taxation, gaining access to resources, and trying to settle old grudges and the multiple historic divisions; posits six scenarios, of which three are seen as “realistic and likely”: “Insurgents as extended arm of ISIS”; “Islamist inspired Mwani rebellion vs Frelimo and Makonde domination”; and “Old claimants to power and resource stakes vs newcomers’ claims”, in which, supported by external security assistance, the Guebuza group would regain power “consolidating the rule of ‘southerners’ and controlling Cabo Delgado’s extractive wealth under the label of national unity.”

a6830.speaker: CMI (Chr Michelsen Institute) paper
a6830.name: CMI (Chr Michelsen Institute) paper
a6830.speech: Points to “the rigorously implemented government ban on any kind of investigation by national journalists and researchers, let alone by an international inquiry. Hence one of the key questions … is, what is the government trying to hide by maintaining, even reinforcing, that ban?”

a6830.speaker: Cabo Ligado weekly report (produced for ACLED by Zitamar and MediaFax, with support from International Crisis Group and USAID)
a6830.name: Cabo Ligado weekly report (produced for ACLED by Zitamar and MediaFax
a6830.title: with support from International Crisis Group and USAID)
a6830.speech: Cited as having the best summary of the Cabo Delgado civil war; the most recent issue details the occupation of Macomia.

a6830.speaker: Miguel de Brito (data source)
a6830.name: Miguel de Brito (data source)
a6830.speech: Provided the Covid-19 data on which the reported case numbers and 7-day moving-average graph are based.

a6881.speaker: Bachir Ousseini, Secretary General of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Niger)
a6881.name: Bachir Ousseini
a6881.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Niger)
a6881.speech: In his address, stated that agriculture is the main provider of employment in Niger, with more than 80% of the population depending on farming and livestock as their principal activities: “These activities, heavily dependent on unstable climatic conditions, also face other constraints including the low level of soil fertility and the low level of use of improved seeds. Indeed, on average less than 4 kilograms per hectare (kg/ha) for fertiliser and a utilisation rate of less than 10% for improved variety seeds.”

a6881.speaker: Bachir Ousseini, Secretary General of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Niger)
a6881.name: Bachir Ousseini
a6881.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Niger)
a6881.speech: Said IFDC’s actions under the ARIA project come at just the right time to support government action in these sectors: “Studies have shown that supplying water through an adequate irrigation system makes it possible to optimise investments in fertiliser and seeds by improving crop yields”, adding that IFDC (International Fertiliser Development Center) has for more than seven years been contributing to this mission carried by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock.

a6881.speaker: Bachir Bounou Issoufa, Country Director of IFDC-Niger
a6881.name: Bachir Bounou Issoufa
a6881.title: Country Director of IFDC-Niger
a6881.speech: Indicated that IFDC’s mission is to develop better technologies for improving soil health and nutrition: “This has undoubtedly led to an increase in the productivity of farms, which strengthens the capacities of rural and urban markets with high-quality agricultural products, accessible to all, especially to low-income consumers”, he explained.

a6881.speaker: Samba Kawa, Director of Agriculture and Resilience at USAID Niger
a6881.name: Samba Kawa
a6881.title: Director of Agriculture and Resilience at USAID Niger
a6881.speech: Recalled that agriculture is the pillar of the Nigerien economy: “That is why the United States government, through USAID, is focusing on improving this sector in order to ensure food security, stimulate economic growth and reduce poverty” ; stressed that the United States government has committed to continuing its support to the agricultural sector initiated by the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC): “Over the next three years, USAID will pay eight (8) million dollars to the ARIA initiative” ; indicated that USAID is committed to sustainable development in Niger and that this meeting would help ensure that the Agricultural Investment Strengthening Support project is well aligned with current policies through the shared vision and priorities of the Nigerien government on agricultural development and food security.

a7084.speaker: Typen Kamanga, MCC Workers Union General Secretary
a7084.name: Typen Kamanga
a7084.title: MCC Workers Union General Secretary
a7084.speech: Said they are demanding a 10 percent salary increase and harmonisation of their pension to 25 percent from the current 10 percent; claimed the council had secretly reduced the pension remittance from 25 percent: “People are very disappointed with the small salary they are receiving and the pension reduction. We want it restored to normal” ; “Authorities are making decisions on their own without involving us. We will not stop protesting until they respond to our demands.”

a7084.speaker: Mcdonald Gondwe, Mzuzu City Council Public Relations Officer
a7084.name: Mcdonald Gondwe
a7084.title: Mzuzu City Council Public Relations Officer
a7084.speech: Said remitting a 25 percent pension contribution is not sustainable given the current financial status of the council; said there is a need to understand the pension remittance dynamics and that the council will engage the workers and provide contingency measures to ensure smooth service delivery: “As the council, we are trying to liaise with them on how best to deal with the matter. The issue largely concerns misunderstanding regarding the pension contribution” ; “It is good for the workers because once they retire, they will be able to receive something, as we will be able to remit contributions to Nico. There will be no problem in increasing salaries because the council will already have settled other mandatory contributions.”

a7087.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a7087.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a7087.title: Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a7087.speech: Has underscored the importance of public-private partnerships in achieving the Ministry's mission of providing integrated, affordable, and responsive healthcare to all Namibians.

a7087.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a7087.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a7087.title: Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a7087.speech: Noted at the opening ceremony of the African Health Workforce Investment Forum on Monday that by the end of 2023, 98.5% of babies born to HIV-positive mothers in Namibia were HIV-free.

a7087.speaker: Zambezi region health directorate
a7087.name: Zambezi region health directorate
a7087.speech: Cited as the source that the Zambezi Region has recorded a worrying increase in malaria cases, with 3,385 cases reported since January and one fatality in August last year.

a7087.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS), Namibia
a7087.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a7087.title: Namibia
a7087.speech: Says the integration of mental health and psychological support within HIV services is key to promoting holistic care, as it will address both mental and physical health as well as improve HIV treatment adherence.

a7087.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS), Namibia
a7087.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a7087.title: Namibia
a7087.speech: Has commended the contractor for the Ombili clinic in Otjiwarongo, which was completed two months ahead of time.

a7087.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS), Namibia
a7087.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a7087.title: Namibia
a7087.speech: Has dismissed rumours circulating false information about the detection of monkeypox (Mpox) disease in Namibia in a social media post.

a7146.speaker: Statement from the Office of the President of South Sudan
a7146.name: Statement from the Office of the President of South Sudan
a7146.speech: "President Kiir expressed his commitment to ensuring a smooth and timely implementation of the extended agreement, noting the availability of resources to support these efforts," said the statement from Kiir's office; it added that the Head of State reassured Amb. Gituai that the country's security situation "remains stable, fostering a conducive environment for the forthcoming general polls." ; according to the statement, the discussions focused on key breakthroughs attained in the ongoing revitalized deal and the preparations for elections in December 2026.

a7146.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a7146.name: Salva Kiir
a7146.title: President of South Sudan
a7146.speech: Assured the chairperson of peace monitoring mechanism R-JMEC of the availability of resources for the 2018 peace implementation.

a7146.speaker: Amb. Charles Tai Gituai, chairperson of the peace monitoring mechanism R-JMEC
a7146.name: Amb. Charles Tai Gituai
a7146.title: chairperson of the peace monitoring mechanism R-JMEC
a7146.speech: Briefed President Kiir on the progress of the agreement implementation, and reportedly highlighted advancements made in the constitution-making process and the security arrangement as critical components of the peace agreement.

a7146.speaker: Khartoum (Government of Sudan)
a7146.name: Khartoum (Government of Sudan)
a7146.speech: Declared force majeure in March 2024, stating it was unable to facilitate the transportation of South Sudan crude oil through the Jabalayn-Port Sudan Pipeline, citing interruptions from the ongoing conflict.

a7146.speaker: Officials from South Sudan and Sudan
a7146.name: Officials from South Sudan and Sudan
a7146.speech: Have repeatedly announced that the damaged pipeline had been repaired and is fully ready for resumption of crude export to the Red Sea.

a7146.speaker: Dr. Martin Lomuro, Cabinet Minister of South Sudan
a7146.name: Dr. Martin Lomuro
a7146.title: Cabinet Minister of South Sudan
a7146.speech: Emphasized the importance of regional and international support for South Sudan's peace process; "Minister Lomuro further stated that the government is prioritizing urgent matters to facilitate the onset of a new transitional period."

a7184.speaker: Vivianne Kibon, International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) operations coordinator
a7184.name: Vivianne Kibon
a7184.title: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) operations coordinator
a7184.speech: has commended Nsanje District Council for properly handling asylum seekers from Mozambique in December 2024 ; said she was pleased that Malawi Red Cross Society used the money for its intended purpose ; “I, therefore, thank Malawi Red Cross Society and Nsanje District Council for a job well done. They complemented the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees' [UNHCR] efforts to improve the welfare of the asylum seekers.”

a7184.speaker: Vivianne Kibon, IFRC operations coordinator for Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe
a7184.name: Vivianne Kibon
a7184.title: IFRC operations coordinator for Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe
a7184.speech: said she was shocked by the United States of America's decision to withdraw support from UNHCR by August this year in the country.

a7184.speaker: Leonard Maganga, Malawi Red Cross acting director
a7184.name: Leonard Maganga
a7184.title: Malawi Red Cross acting director
a7184.speech: thanked IFRC and DG-Eco who supported them to provide humanitarian assistance to the refugees.

a7184.speaker: Dominic Mwandira, Nsanje District Commissioner
a7184.name: Dominic Mwandira
a7184.title: Nsanje District Commissioner
a7184.speech: said his staff showed commitment to work with the asylum seekers. “Most of the asylum seekers arrived on Christmas Eve when we were on holiday but we came back to the office to work.”

a7219.speaker: Ministry of Health of South Sudan (official Facebook page)
a7219.name: Ministry of Health of South Sudan (official Facebook page)
a7219.speech: According to the Ministry of Health’s official Facebook Page, diplomat Michael J Adler reiterated the pressing need for the government to increase public revenue to strengthen health facilities.

a7219.speaker: Michael J. Adler, U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan
a7219.name: Michael J. Adler
a7219.title: U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan
a7219.speech: Met health Minister Yolanda Awel and discussed the critical role of USAID in supporting health centers across South Sudan; reiterated the pressing need for the government to increase public revenue to strengthen health facilities ; The Ambassador also emphasized the call on the government to pay it employees salaries and reduced risks for dedicated aid workers serving the South Sudanese population.

a7219.speaker: Yolanda Awel Deng, Minister of Health of South Sudan
a7219.name: Yolanda Awel Deng
a7219.title: Minister of Health of South Sudan
a7219.speech: Highlighted the ongoing reforms with funding collaborations with partners, including USAID, which is the largest contributor to the health sector services ; She reportedly emphasized the importance of outreach services to health centers nationwide, acknowledging the challenges faced within the ministry, including difficult working conditions for some staff members ; Yolanda expressed her commitment to collaborating closely with the South Sudanese government, partners, and donors, including USAID, to ensure the health sector is adequately supported and that the welfare of health workers is prioritized.

a7292.speaker: Hamas (statement)
a7292.name: Hamas (statement)
a7292.speech: The Palestinian movement said in a statement that Netanyahu's decision to suspend humanitarian aid to Gaza is “low-level blackmail, a war crime and a flagrant violation of the agreement” ; Netanyahu's decision, according to Hamas, to suspend humanitarian aid to Gaza is “cheap blackmail, a war crime and a flagrant strike against the agreement.”

a7292.speaker: Hamas (statement)
a7292.name: Hamas (statement)
a7292.speech: Said on Sunday that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had gone back on the Gaza ceasefire agreement by adopting an American proposal aimed at extending the first phase of the agreement, calling on the mediators to exert pressure to begin negotiations on the second phase ; The movement said that “the statement issued by the office of the prime minister of the terrorist occupation government, Netanyahu, concerning his adoption of the American proposals aimed at extending the first phase of the agreement, on terms that violate the Gaza ceasefire agreement, is a flagrant attempt to circumvent the agreement and to avoid entering into negotiations for its second phase.”

a7292.speaker: Hamas (statement)
a7292.name: Hamas (statement)
a7292.speech: Called on the mediators and the international community to act “to pressure the Israeli occupation and put an end to its punitive and immoral measures against more than two million people in the Gaza Strip” ; The Palestinian movement called on the mediators to “pressure the occupation so that it respects its obligations under the agreement, at all its stages, that it implement the humanitarian protocol and that it bring shelters and rescue material into the Gaza Strip.”

a7292.speaker: Hamas (statement)
